chunks.title: Can I edit videos in this product?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I edit videos in this product?
Yes — in the **media/content module**. A video is a "content piece". First you need a video to edit: either
generate one with AI (from a brief → script → scenes) or import/upload your own clips. Then open the piece and
use the **Video timeline editor**: reorder/trim scenes, change transitions (cut/fade/crossfade), split or
delete a scene, refine a selected time-range with AI, and balance the **audio track** (voiceover + music
volume/duck) with a live waveform. Steps: open a content piece → "Timeline editor" → edit → Save.

chunks.title: Can I make a video with AI from just an idea/topic?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I make a video with AI from just an idea/topic?
Yes. In the content module, create a piece from a **brief** (a plain-language topic). The pipeline chains:
generate a **script** (beats) → **voiceover** (ElevenLabs) → **visuals** (per scene: AI video-gen via fal, or
images for a slideshow) → **assemble** into a real `.mp4` with ffmpeg. You approve cost/gates along the way
(the human accepts; the Conductor executes — single-writer). Without provider keys it still runs on
valid-shaped stubs so you can rehearse the flow.

chunks.title: Can I edit images?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I edit images?
Yes — the **image editor** in the media module (open an image asset on a content piece). It does brightness/
contrast/saturation, one-tap look filters (grayscale/sepia), a draggable text overlay, **crop + resize** to a
preset, and a **side-by-side compare** (original vs edited). The edit is exported as a NEW image asset
(non-destructive — the original stays).

chunks.title: Can I make longer videos (e.g. several minutes)?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I make longer videos (e.g. several minutes)?
Yes, via **scene decomposition**: the idea is split into N scenes that flow into each other (continuity
prompts), one AI-generated clip per scene, stitched with transitions. Video length ≈ number of scenes × per-
scene duration; the media budget is the practical cap. A duration target ("short / long") plans the number of
beats/scenes.

chunks.title: Can I refine just one part of a video (e.g. seconds 13–18)?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I refine just one part of a video (e.g. seconds 13–18)?
Yes — in the timeline editor, select a time-range and "Refine selection" with an instruction; only the covered
scene(s) are regenerated as a new version (the rest is untouched).

chunks.title: Can I add or balance audio (voiceover + background music)?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I add or balance audio (voiceover + background music)?
Yes — the timeline editor has an **audio track**: it shows a waveform for the voiceover and the music, with a
**voice-volume** slider and a **music-duck** slider. The saved mix is applied when the video is rendered
(voice + ducked music mixed into one track).

chunks.title: Can I generate a voiceover / music / sound effects?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I generate a voiceover / music / sound effects?
Yes — voiceover and SFX via **ElevenLabs**, music via **Suno**, all through the media providers. They attach
to a content piece as assets and feed the render.

chunks.title: Can I publish a video to YouTube or TikTok?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I publish a video to YouTube or TikTok?
Yes — connect the platform account first (content settings → connect), then on a finished (non-stub) render
click Publish and pick the platform. YouTube uses a resumable byte-upload; TikTok uses async status polling. A
publish only lands as "done" when the account is really connected; otherwise it is honestly marked as a stub.

## Design & Studio module

chunks.title: Can I design a UI theme / pick a style?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I design a UI theme / pick a style?
Yes — the **Designer module**. It has themes (colour palette, light+dark), styles (component language: radius/
shadow/fonts/density/motion — e.g. Apple, Material, Glassmorphic), animations, and typography. You can AI-
generate a theme/style from a brief, preview it live, pick from premade catalog entries, and "Use in project"
to apply it (it becomes the design-system context the coding agent follows).

chunks.title: Can I upload or customize my own theme/style?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I upload or customize my own theme/style?
Yes — duplicate a premade or generated theme, rename + edit its tokens, delete your own (premades are read-
only), and import/export a theme as JSON. Changes persist to your workspace.

## Dev-orchestration module (software projects)

chunks.title: Can I build software / a new project?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I build software / a new project?
Yes — the **dev module**. Create a project (link an existing git repo, or **greenfield** from a stack
template which initialises a real repo with a runnable seed file-tree). Tickets move across an AI pipeline
(refine → plan → implement → test → review); the code-writing agent runs in a Docker container. You approve;
the Conductor executes.

chunks.title: Can I preview or deploy my app?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I preview or deploy my app?
Yes — a per-ticket preview container, and persistent environments (dev/staging/prod). A **demo** environment
serves `main` at a stable URL and can auto-redeploy when main moves; a **prod build-export** produces a real
build tarball + fires a deploy-hook to an external server.

chunks.title: Can the AI ask me questions while working?
chunks.text:
Q: Can the AI ask me questions while working?
Yes — a stage can park on a **needs-input** question that surfaces as a structured approve/reject/choice card
(phone-usable). You answer; the parked turn resumes with your answer.

## Workspace-AI (the assistant)

chunks.title: What can the Workspace-AI assistant do?
chunks.text:
Q: What can the Workspace-AI assistant do?
It proposes actions from a plain-language request — create a ticket, create a content piece, move/assign
tickets, add a comment, or a multi-step plan — as a **proposal you accept** (it never writes state directly;
the Conductor is the single writer). It grounds on the workspace snapshot + your linked code (RAG) + (Q-fase)
the product's own capabilities.

chunks.title: Does the AI know my codebase / uploaded media?
chunks.text:
Q: Does the AI know my codebase / uploaded media?
Yes — the linked repo is indexed for retrieval (RAG), so the coding agent + the assistant ground on the actual
code; uploaded media becomes content assets the pipeline uses.

## Sources / knowledge / RAG

chunks.title: Can I give the AI extra context or docs?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I give the AI extra context or docs?
Yes — add **Sources** (context-docs, per-channel brand voice); they're indexed and injected into the relevant
AI stages. The repo is indexed on merge; you can re-scan the index.

## Accounts & channels

chunks.title: Can I manage multiple social accounts / channels?
chunks.text:
Q: Can I manage multiple social accounts / channels?
Channels carry a platform + brand voice; a content piece bound to a channel grounds its generation on that
channel's brand. Connecting and routing publishes to a specific account is what the account-management surface
provides.

chunks.title: 0002-fase1-inprocess-conductor
chunks.text: ADR 0002: 0002-fase1-inprocess-conductor. `CONTROL_API.md` (§3/§7) specifies that every user-initiated write goes: `_api` route → `preApiExecute` RBAC → **append a `WorkspaceSignal` to a Redis-backed serial signal-log** → the **single-instance Conductor** (running in the separate orchestrator process under `lease:orchestrator`) drains it and writes. That async signal-log + lease exists to keep the write path safe across the **web-app ↔ orchestrator process split** (the web-app scales horizontally; the orchestrator is single-instance). Fase 1 (basisplatform, no AI) ships the non-AI control-API ops (workspace/member/ RBAC/settings/board CRUD) BEFORE the orchestrator process exists — that process, its lease, the PTY/container engine, and the Redis drain loop are all Fase 2 (Lane A, spike-gated). If Fase 1 handlers enqueued to a Redis signal-log, nothing would drain it (no Conductor process yet) and nothing would persist. Decision: **In Fase 1 the control-API handler enqueues to an IN-PROCESS serial Conductor executor** (a single-writer promise-chain/mutex inside the one running web-app/dev process), which executes each op via `tenantDb` under `runInTenant(workspaceId)`. The **Redis-backed signal-log + `lease:orchestrator` + the out-of-process drain loop land in Fase 2** when the orchestrator process actually splits out (Lane A, A3). The `ControlRequest`/`ControlAck` contract and the enqueue→Conductor→`ws-ai:*` shape are unchanged — only the *transport* of the enqueue (in-memory

chunks.title: 0004-app-owned-secret-encryption
chunks.text: ADR 0004: 0004-app-owned-secret-encryption. Workspaces stores credentials it must replay to third parties — first the per-workspace GitLab token (`Workspace.gitlabTokenEnc`), later others. These cannot be one-way hashed (they must be decrypted to use) and must not sit in the DB as plaintext (B-07). The `@luckystack/secret-manager` resolves *deploy-time* env pointers at boot; it is not a per-row, per-tenant, runtime write-path for user-entered credentials, so it doesn't fit. Decision: Encrypt these secrets in the app with **AES-256-GCM**, in `server/crypto/secretBox.ts` (`encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret`), keyed by a single app key from `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` (any string, SHA-256-hashed to 32 bytes; resolved at boot like any env, so it can be a secret-manager pointer). Stored format is self-describing: `v1:<iv>:<tag>:<ct>` (base64). The **Conductor** is the only writer (B-23) — `gitlab-settings` encrypts on write; a Fase-2 GitLab client decrypts on use. When `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` is unset, secrets are stored `plain:<b64>` with a loud one-time boot warning. This keeps local dev frictionless while making the unencrypted state obvious + greppable; `decryptSecret` reads both forms, so setting the key later is non-breaking for new writes.

chunks.title: 0005-per-action-typed-api-write-routes
chunks.text: ADR 0005: 0005-per-action-typed-api-write-routes. The single `workspaces/control` route took a `Record<string, unknown>` transport envelope (`{ op, target, payload }`) and dispatched by `op` inside the Conductor. Because the client-facing payloads were untyped, the generated type-map (the "type-server") could not type any write call — the item-9 complaint: *"in de payloads gewoon record<string,unknown> waardoor onze typing server geen nut heeft… liefst voor iedere actie een eigen api call."* The user's stated direction was: per-action calls, **and** "eigenlijk moet bijna alles sync calls worden" — use `_sync` events for in-workspace realtime writes, with the client merging on `seq`. This decision was taken during an unattended overnight `/loop`: the AI can run tsc/lint/build + code-direct Mongo integration tests, but **cannot drive a browser**, so any Socket.io/`_sync` room-fanout + client-merge path is unverifiable this session. Investigation also showed the client room-join API (`joinRoom`) is not cleanly surfaced, and `sync.requireRoomMembership` defaults to `true` (0.2.0) — a `_sync` write path has moving parts that only a browser can prove. Decision: **Split the write path into one typed `_api` route per action** (`quickAdd_v1`, `sprintCreate_v1`, …), each with a fully-typed `ApiParams.data` payload, so the generated type-map types the client's `apiRequest({ name: 'workspaces/<op>', … })` call end-to-end. Each route stays thin: validate → `hasCapability` RBAC (the shared

chunks.title: 0006-realtime-sync-delta-transport
chunks.text: ADR 0006: 0006-realtime-sync-delta-transport. ADR 0005 split the write path into per-action typed `_api` routes but kept realtime as refetch-on-write, explicitly deferring the `_sync` delta layer to a browser-testable session ("This ADR is superseded if/when the `_sync` layer lands"). In practice the refetch model meant a user had to reload the board to see a new ticket ("ik moet een page refresh doen wat echt niet fatsoenlijk is") — realtime is a V1 requirement, and the user asked for **separate events per action** ("aparte events voor iedere verschillende actie"), with clients **merging deltas, never refetching**. The session now has agent-browser + Playwright MCP available, and the client room-join API (`joinRoom`/`leaveRoom` from `src/_sockets/socketInitializer`) + `syncRequest` / `useSyncEvents` are usable — the moving parts ADR 0005 flagged as unverifiable are now verifiable. Decision: **Every in-workspace write is a per-action `_sync` event that broadcasts its DELTA to the workspace room (room code = workspaceId); every client — including the sender — merges the delta into local state via `upsertSyncEventCallback`. No refetch.** - Each op keeps its OWN `_sync` route + event name (`workspaces/quickAdd`, `workspaces/bulkMove`, …) — the "separate events per action" ask. chunks.title: 0008-container-runtime-model
chunks.text: ADR 0008: 0008-container-runtime-model. Lane F's P1 scope is "L1 base image + provisioning skeleton" (`07b §1`). Building it surfaced concrete implementation choices the design doc (`07b`) frames but does not pin, and one it explicitly warns about (`§4`). This records the choices made in the phase-3 container spine, so a later session doesn't re-litigate them. Decision: - **Worktree = `git clone --single-branch` into a container-owned volume, NOT a bind-mount of the host `git worktree` checkout** (`07b §4`, Q-CT-WORKTREE). A git worktree's `.git` is a *gitdir pointer* back to the main repo; bind-mounting only the worktree dir leaves a dangling pointer that breaks git on the first command inside the container. The clone is self-contained. The `DEV-####` branch (cut at the frozen commit in phase 1b) is the clone's `--branch`, so its tip IS the frozen commit — no detaching checkout. - **`git config --system safe.directory '*'` is BAKED into L1.** The RO `/mirror` (host clone) is host-uid-owned; git's dubious-ownership guard refuses it. `-c safe.directory` is ignored by git for this key BY DESIGN — only system/global config is honored — so it must live in the image. - **Name-based idempotency, no persistence yet.** A container is keyed by `ws-<safe(workspaceId)>-<safe(ticketKey)>`; re-activation reuses/ restarts the named container. chunks.title: 0009-register-flow-ai-operations
chunks.text: ADR 0009: 0009-register-flow-ai-operations. Register-flow steps C (AI `.workspaces/Dockerfile`) and D (AI docs) are the first AI *write-ish* operations — each drives a slow `claude` turn (~30-120s) that produces a project artifact. Three cross-cutting choices settled while building them (phases 6a/6b). Decision: - **AI operations are direct `_api` routes, NOT Conductor control-ops.** `generateDockerfile` / `generateProjectDoc` / `aiChat` each run a multi-second-to-minute AI turn. The Conductor is the single SERIAL writer for authoritative state; routing a 2-minute turn through it would stall every other write. So AI ops call the provider layer directly from an `_api` handler (capability-gated), and only their *result* — if it mutates state — goes through a normal control-op (e.g. the Workspace-AI chat's accepted proposal dispatches `bulk-move`). - **Generated artifacts are a reviewable DRAFT, never auto-applied.** The Dockerfile is written to `data/workspaces/<id>/draft.Dockerfile` and validated to extend the L1 base (`FROM workspaces/base` only, Q-CT-DOCKERFILE-TRUST) — but NOT built or committed. The user reviews (Monaco slice) before it becomes the repo's `.workspaces/Dockerfile` and an L2 image. Docs land as `generated` InfoSources the user can see + toggle, not silent truth. - **Pure-context prompting.** The `claude-cli` provider runs in a scratch cwd (not a repo checkout), so AI-gen prompts pass the repo content inline (manifests + file tree) and explicitly forbid files

chunks.title: 0010-per-container-editor-with-user-profile
chunks.text: ADR 0010: 0010-per-container-editor-with-user-profile. The V1 code editor is the real browser VS Code (openvscode-server), per [CODE_EDITOR.md] and the hybrid decision ([[workspaces-editor-plan]]): Monaco for lightweight embedded surfaces, openvscode-server for the full editor. An open question was *where* the full editor runs: - **Central editor + git worktrees** — one openvscode-server on the host that opens each ticket's worktree folder. Cheap, no per-ticket container for the editor, and extension logins persist for free (one shared user-data-dir). But the editor's LSP / "run" / integrated terminal only see the HOST toolchain, not the project's — so a Python/Go/… project gets no working IntelliSense, no in-project terminal, no per-project toolchain, unless the host happens to have every toolchain. - **Per-container editor** — openvscode-server INSIDE each ticket container (07b / [0008]). The editor sees exactly the project's L2 toolchain + installed deps + the agent's worktree, so LSP, "run", terminal, and extensions all work against the real project. Costs +300–800 MB/session and each container has its OWN filesystem, so extension installs + auth logins do NOT carry across tickets/workspaces by default. chunks.text: ADR 0011: 0011-pluggable-proxy-and-git-workflow-config. Two related customization needs surfaced for Workspaces V1: 1. **Git/workflow** — teams name branches differently (`DEV-1240` vs `feature/DEV-1240-…`), have different push/MR policies, and want to steer *how* the AI commits ("split a ticket into testable steps, commit each passing step"). The runtime hardcoded `branch == ticket key` in three places (worktree, container, host). 2. **Preview hosting** — each ticket's container is exposed at a per-ticket subdomain of `workspace.<domain>` (wildcard DNS + cert). The user runs **nginx** today but Caddy is the easier fit for per-ticket route churn. An editor-specific Caddy driver already existed (`caddyRoutes.ts`), but nothing general or pluggable. The forces: the reverse proxy is an integration point (not core logic); branch/host derivation must be deterministic (code parses it); but "how to commit" is prose the AI interprets, not something code enforces. We needed a principled line so customization doesn't become a grab-bag. Decision: **A. The line = "does CODE act on it, or does the AI just READ it?"** - **Code acts → structured config.** A per-workspace `GitConfig` (`Workspace.gitConfig` JSON): `branchStrategy` (ticket-prefix | typed | custom template), `pushPolicy`, `targetBranch`, `protectedBranches`, `commitSigning`. `server/git/branchStrategy.ts` is the pure resolver: `resolveBranchName` (called once at branch creation, persisted on `Ticket.branch`) + `deriveHostSlug` (

chunks.text: ADR 0012: 0012-editor-engine-edit-lock-and-proxy-boot-reconcile. Two systems now touch a ticket's container + its `/work` git-worktree: - the **autonomous engine** (`stageRunner` drives an in-container `claude` turn that edits + commits on `/work`), and - the **per-ticket live editor** (openvscode-server, ADR 0010, edits the same `/work`). Running both at once races the worktree — the AI could commit on top of a human's unsaved edits, or vice-versa. `CODE_EDITOR_BUILD_PLAN` Track C4 (`userEditable` edit-lock) was schema-only and UNENFORCED. Separately, per-ticket proxy routes (`server/proxy`, ADR 0011) outlive a backend restart: after a crash/redeploy a `ws-route-*` can point at a container that is gone. The editor open-flow lives in another agent's files (`editorSession.ts`, `openEditor_v1.ts`); the engine + proxy are this side's. So the guard is built where it can be enforced without racing that work, and the editor-side half is offered as a ready helper to call. Decision: **A. Mutual edit-lock (`server/orchestrator/editGuard.ts`).** - **Engine side (enforced, `conductor.provisionContainers`):** before auto-running a stage turn, `isEditorRunning(workspaceId, ticketKey)` checks for a live openvscode-server process in the container; if present, the turn is **skipped + logged** (re-entering the stage re-triggers it). The engine never clobbers a human's open session. - **Editor side (`ticketEditGuard`, a helper the open-flow calls):** refuse to open the editor when the current

chunks.text: ADR 0013: 0013-engine-control-plane-completion. The autonomous engine ran tickets to a committed branch, but the loop wasn't closed: the AI's work never left the container (commits were local-only), a runaway turn couldn't be stopped, the engine's stage-advance was silent (boards only updated on reload), and there was no way to see a ticket's app running. This ADR records the batch of control-plane decisions that close those gaps (CODE_EDITOR Track C/F + the realtime + preview layers), built engine/conductor/proxy-side while another agent built the editor/Caddy/UI side. Decision: **A. Push-on-approval (Track F) — `server/git/forge.ts`.** When a `done` turn leaves a stage that gates for approval OR is terminal, and the workspace `pushPolicy` ≠ `local-only`, push the ticket branch to origin and (for `merge-request`) open/find a GitLab MR against `targetBranch`. The GitLab token is decrypted ONLY in forge, injected transiently (git `withAuth` url + the MR `PRIVATE-TOKEN` header), never stored/logged; `protectedBranches` are refused. Fired fire-and-forget from the stage-runner so a slow/failed forge never breaks the turn. **B. Agent controls (C2) — `pause`/`resume`/`kill`/`pause-all`/`resume-all`.** `pause` is a PROVISIONING flag, not a freeze of a running turn: per-ticket `Ticket.status='paused'` and workspace `Workspace.paused` make `provisionContainers` skip. `kill` stops an in-flight turn by killing the in-container `claude` PROCPS-FREE (walk `/proc/[pid]/cmdline`; ps/pgrep a

chunks.title: 0014-market-hardening-gitlab-ingestion-capacity-edge-auth
chunks.text: ADR 0014: 0014-market-hardening-gitlab-ingestion-capacity-edge-auth. Toward market readiness, four gaps remained on the engine/proxy side: the board was NOT fed from the source (tickets came from quick-add, not GitLab issues — `gitlab-resync` was a no-op); nothing capped concurrent autonomous turns (runaway container spawning under load); the editor/preview subdomains were protected only by the openvscode connection token (no session gate); and error tracking was installed but inactive. This ADR records the batch closing them. Decision: **A. GitLab issue ingestion — `server/git/gitlabSync.ts` + the `gitlab-resync` op.** Pull the linked project's open issues via the GitLab REST API (reusing the forge token model: decrypt only here, `PRIVATE-TOKEN` header) and upsert them as tickets keyed `DEV-<iid>`. NEW issues enter at `unrefined` (the AI moves them on); EXISTING tickets get title/labels/description refreshed WITHOUT touching their pipeline position. The op broadcasts the touched tickets so the board updates live. This is the ingestion half of the loop (a webhook-driven continuous sync + a push-back of AI state to GitLab remain Fase-2 follow-ups). **B. CapacityManager — a host-wide concurrent-turn cap.** `provisionContainers` defers a turn (banner + broadcast, stays in-stage) when `busy worker AgentSessions >= WS_MAX_CONCURRENT_TURNS` (default 4). A completing turn frees a slot; re-entering the stage runs it. Deliberately a SOFT cap — a simultaneous burst can race past it, bu

chunks.title: 0015-multi-instance-safety-deel-a
chunks.text: ADR 0015: 0015-multi-instance-safety-deel-a. The engine's authoritative-write path (the Conductor) was built single-instance: a global in-process promise chain (`chain`) serialised all writes, an in-process `Set` deduped re-sends, and the GitLab poller + editor reaper ran on `setInterval` in every process. Running 2+ instances behind the router would give: concurrent authoritative writes on the same workspace (races, double AI-turns on one container), un-deduped re-sends across instances, an unboundedly growing dedup Set, and N× duplicated background work. The user chose to do this RIGHT ONCE now — not because scale is here, but because the single-instance assumption is baked into the engine core and is far cheaper to remove now than to retrofit after more code depends on it. Scope = **Deel A: make the engine multi-instance-SAFE while still running one instance** (spinning up N later is then config, "Deel B", not a rewrite). Redis is already a hard dependency (session, `nextSignalSeq` via `redis.incr`, rate-limit), and the framework already exposes lease primitives (`acquireLease`/`renewLease`/`releaseLease`, atomic `SET NX PX`) and a socket Redis adapter — so this is wiring existing primitives, not greenfield. chunks.title: 0016-egress-control
chunks.text: ADR 0016: 0016-egress-control. A worker container runs code the AI writes plus a repo's dependencies — not fully trusted, and a single malicious npm/pip package can exfiltrate. Until now workers ran on the default bridge with FULL outbound network: they could POST secrets (env, the projected `~/.claude` creds, tokens) or the repo's code to any host, reach internal services, or abuse the host (mining/spam). That is the top blocker to letting customers trust their private code to the platform. Decision: Opt-in egress control (`WS_EGRESS=1`, default OFF ⇒ current behaviour unchanged). New `server/container/egress.ts`; `launchTicketContainer` calls `ensureEgressInfra()` and adds `egressLaunchArgs()` when enabled: - **Isolation** — the worker joins `ws-egress`, an `--internal` docker network with NO route out. - **Allowlist proxy** — a squid container sits on BOTH `ws-egress` and a normal network, so it (and only it) bridges outward; the worker's `HTTP(S)_PROXY` points at it. squid ACLs allow CONNECT/GET only to a domain allowlist (npm/yarn/pip/crates, GitHub/GitLab/googlesource, OS repos, the AI APIs), extendable via `WS_EGRESS_ALLOW`; everything else is denied. Domain-level, no MITM. Verified against real Docker (`scripts/spike/egressSpike.mts`): an allowlisted domain (github.com) returns 200 through the proxy, a non-allowlisted one (example.com) is blocked, and a direct request with no proxy has no route at all (isolation).

chunks.title: 0020-capacity-manager-hard-cap
chunks.text: ADR 0020: 0020-capacity-manager-hard-cap. Goal-item #12. The old CapacityManager (ADR 0014) was a **soft** cap: `provisionContainers` did `agentSession.count({ status: 'busy' }) >= MAX` and deferred above it. Between the count and `runStage`, N concurrent stage-activations all read the same "3 busy" and each start a 4th turn — a classic TOCTOU that a burst races straight past. N concurrent acquires can no longer all pass — the cap is hard. - **Urgent force-through:** `priority === 'urgent'` passes `force = true` — always admitted, but still tracked in the active set so normal tickets see true occupancy (an urgent turn does consume a real slot for everyone else). chunks.text: ADR 0021: 0021-real-git-merge. Goal-item #9. The built-in MR review (ADR 0018) could open/diff/comment/approve an MR, but `mergeMr` was a **status flip only** — it set `status='merged'` without touching git. That's a lie: the target branch never actually received the work, and there was no rollback. On conflict the merge is **aborted** (target untouched) and the conflicting files are returned. `revertMergeCommit` rolls a merge back with a history-preserving **git-revert** (auto `-m 1` for a real merge commit, plain revert for a squash), never a destructive reset. - **Serial by the existing lease.** Merges run inside the Conductor's op switch, which already holds the per-workspace write-lease (ADR 0015), so two merges can't race the same target. chunks.text: ADR 0029: 0029-forge-provider-abstraction. Goal-item #10. chunks.title: 0030-editor-loose-ends
chunks.text: ADR 0030: 0030-editor-loose-ends. Goal-item #14 groups four editor "loose ends": editor-profile encryption-at-rest, Open VSX extensions, committing the generated Dockerfile into the repo, and Monaco i18n. Two are self- contained security/correctness wins that don't collide with the concurrent editor UI work; two are larger and are scoped honestly below. Decision: - **Editor-profile encryption-at-rest** (the security-critical one). The per-user editor profile carries openvscode's SECRET STORAGE — extension **auth tokens** — and was stored as loose plaintext files under `data/editor-profiles/<userId>/`. Now each half (user-data, extensions) is captured out of the container as a tar, **AES-256-GCM encrypted** (`secretBox.encryptBuffer`, same app key as the GitLab-token encryption), and written as a `.tar.enc` blob; on the next session it is decrypted + streamed back in. Kinds → roles/features: landing+brand = `designer`/`studio-designer`, copy+strategy = `marketer`/`studio-marketer` (two new `AiFeature`s + assignments, defaulting to claude-cli, overridable to gemini per the abstraction). Landing = a self-contained responsive HTML page (rendered in a **sandboxed iframe** — no scripts run); brand/copy = structured JSON; strategy = markdown. - **AgentRole bridge** (`server/studio/roles.ts`): registers `studio-designer` + `studio-marketer` into the #2 registry (`mutates: true` →

chunks.title: 0034-tool-module-pipeline-coupling
chunks.text: ADR 0034: 0034-tool-module-pipeline-coupling. The Designer, standalone Interviewer, and Marketing/Studio surfaces were built as **standalone tool-modules**: the Designer's themes/styles/animations are client-only React state (lost on reload, no Prisma model); the standalone Interviewer chat is ephemeral (`workspaces/aiChat`) and its agent-role output is **notification-only**; Studio artifacts persist but link to nothing. Meanwhile the pipeline feeds the in-container coding `claude` agent **only** through `InfoSource` context-docs (`sourceIds` → `renderStage` → `/work/CLAUDE.md`) + RAG excerpts (`stageRunner.runStage`). The user decided (2026-07-05) to couple them, with the active design choice held **workspace-wide** (not per-ticket). Decision: 1. **Design-system is the coupling.** Persist the Designer library as `DesignArtifact` rows (kind `theme|style|animation`, `active` flag). One **active theme + style per workspace** is the fixed truth; the Designer stays a playground. From the active choice we synthesize a single `InfoSource(mode:'context-doc', source:'design-system', name:'Design system')`; `stageRunner` auto-injects `source:'design-system'` into **every** stage's `CLAUDE.md` (same seam as `source:'starter'`). chunks.title: 0035-multi-project-multi-service
chunks.text: ADR 0035: 0035-multi-project-multi-service. D12 (`features/01_WORKSPACE_SETUP.md` §Resolved / `features/INDEX.md`) locked **one project = one workspace**: the setup wizard stays single-project, there is no project switcher, and the seed's second project (`youcomm-api`) is "legacy". That was the right V1 simplification, but it blocks the user's real case — *"a Java backend separate from an HTML frontend; 2 repos together OR separate, and services instead of one monorepo."* CLAUDE.md already records the product is "EXPANDING past the old single-* V1", and the Expansion Program's item **A1** makes multi-project the tent-pole everything else (deploy, environments, per-project forge) hangs off. The codebase is already **structurally** multi-project: `Project.@@index([workspaceId])` is NOT unique; `Ticket`, `PipelineStage`, `MergeRequest` already carry a required `projectId`; `InfoSource`/`RagEntry`/ `StudioBrief` carry an optional `projectId`; `WorkspaceTrigger.match` already has a `projectIds[]` filter; and the bootstrap helpers (`defaultPipeline`, `starterLibrary`) already take an explicit `projectId`. The single-project assumption lives almost entirely in **one runtime pattern** — `project.findFirst({ where: { workspaceId } })` (≈15 callsites) plus three dangerous `updateMany({ where: { workspaceId } })` fan-outs — and in the **client**, which has no "current project" concept at all. Decision: Reverse D12. A workspace holds **N projects** (polyrepo); a project optionally declar

chunks.title: 0036-github-forge-per-project
chunks.text: ADR 0036: 0036-github-forge-per-project. `FORGE_ABSTRACTION.md` designs a 6-capability `ForgeProvider` seam (boardSync / repoHosting / mergeRequests / ci / webhooks / auth) across GitLab / GitHub / Builtin, but only **GitLab is built**, and the live implementation is lighter than the doc's design: there is NO `ForgeProvider` interface in code — forge state lives on `Workspace` (`forgeType` = `'gitlab' | 'github'`, `gitlabUrl`, `gitlabTokenEnc`, `gitConfig`), resolved inline in `server/git/forge.ts` (`asForgeType`, `forgeBase`). A two-provider MR request-shaper (`server/git/forgeProvider.ts`, `openForgeMergeRequest`) already branches `gitlab` vs `github` for the merge-request/PR call; issue ingestion (`gitlabSync.ts`) and webhook parsing (`webhookIngest.ts`) are GitLab-only. Forge is **per-workspace**, and the on-disk bare clone (`repoStore.ts`) is keyed by `workspaceId`. The Expansion Program item **A2** un-defers GitHub, and ADR 0035 (A1) made a workspace hold N projects. So the forge must become **per-project** (a workspace can mix a GitLab backend project and a GitHub frontend project), and the physical repo — deferred by A1 — must be re-keyed per project. Decision: 1. **Per-project `ForgeConnection`** (`mode` `'gitlab' | 'github'`, `baseUrl`, `repoPath`, `tokenEnc`, `webhookSecret`, `status`; `@@unique([projectId])`). This adapts the doc's `ForgeConnection` (which was per-workspace) to per-project — **forced by A1**; the builtin-mode fields (`builtinRepoRef`, `ciRunner`)

chunks.title: 0037-environments-persistent-server
chunks.text: ADR 0037: 0037-environments-persistent-server. Everything that runs a user's app today is EPHEMERAL: the 30-min ticket preview (`previewSession.ts`) launches a per-ticket container behind `<branch-slug>.<domain>` and is reaped with the ticket. There is no long-running deployment — nothing that serves a project's app at a stable URL after Review. B1 adds the first persistent run target: `dev` / `staging` / `prod` environments, each a long-running container at a STABLE route, reusing the existing substrate (`launchTicketContainer` + the proxy abstraction + `imageBuild`'s `Project.baseImageRef`). No `Environment`/`Deployment` model existed (schema §18 even bars adding preview-deploy models in V1) — this is the first. Decision: 1. **`Environment` model** (`workspaceId`, `projectId`, `serviceId?`, `kind`, `route`, `imageRef?`, `containerName?`, `branch?`, `status`, `healthUrl?`, `lastError?`, `lastDeployedAt?`). One environment per (project, service, kind); `serviceId` null = the project root (single-service repo). Uniqueness is enforced in the deploy op (Mongo nullable-unique is unreliable), not a `@@unique`. 2. **A persistent env is `previewSession` minus the TTL, plus a stable route + readiness.** `deployEnvironment` launches a container via `launchTicketContainer` with a synthetic stable key `env-<envId>` cloning the DEPLOY branch (gitConfig.targetBranch, default `main`) rather than a ticket branch, runs the serve command (`Service.devCommand ?? Project.devCommand ?? 'npm run

chunks.title: 0038-deploy-cd-downloadable-builds
chunks.text: ADR 0038: 0038-deploy-cd-downloadable-builds. B1 (ADR 0037) added persistent environments + `deployEnvironment`. B2 turns that into a CD flow: move a tested build UP the fixed `dev → staging → prod` ladder (gated), and let the user EXPORT a build to self-host elsewhere — the user's explicit ask: *"optie 1 [same-host deploy] maar we willen ook builds kunnen downloaden om die zelf ergens anders te hosten."* Decision: 1. **Promote ladder (`env-promote`).** `promoteEnvironment(project, service, fromKind, {approved})` deploys the next stage with the SOURCE env's EXACT image pinned (`deployEnvironment(..., {imageRef})`) — what you tested on dev is what ships, not a fresh branch pull. Gates: the source must be **live** (a health signal — you can't promote a broken build), and **prod requires an explicit approval** (B-23 confirm). The green-CI gate is a documented HOOK that C1 (BUILTIN_CI) fills — left as an explicit TODO in `promote.ts` rather than faking a check that doesn't exist yet. 2. **Downloadable build export (`build-export` + `BuildArtifact`).** `buildExport` runs `docker save` on the project's built image → an OCI tarball under the workspace data dir, tracked by a `BuildArtifact` row (building→ready|error) with an unguessable 24-byte `downloadToken` + a TTL. Served over a signed, TTL'd, token-gated link `GET /downloads/build/<token>` (origin-exempt, streamed, 404 on unknown/expired — no existence oracle). The `bundle` kind (built dist, not the whole image) is deferred to t

chunks.title: 0039-builtin-ci-quality-gates
chunks.text: ADR 0039: 0039-builtin-ci-quality-gates. B2 (ADR 0038) left an explicit TODO: the prod-promote gate needs a green-CI check "once BUILTIN_CI lands". C1 un-defers `BUILTIN_CI_PIPELINES.md` (a designed-but-deferred spec) to build that: a CI job DAG on the existing orchestrator where a **red required job blocks merge/promote**. No CI models/parser/runner existed — only the two gate hooks I left (the `mr-merge` merge point + the prod-promote `ciGreen` TODO). Decision: 1. **Three models, exactly per BUILTIN_CI §9** — `Pipeline` (a project's `.workspaces/ci.yml` definition, one active per project), `PipelineRun` (one execution at a frozen commit; `status` gates), `PipelineJob` (one job = a container exec). ⚠ `Pipeline` is UNRELATED to `PipelineStage` (board columns) — same word, different concept; the schema carries a loud comment. 2. **"Borrowed, not built" runner** — `runPipeline` reads `.workspaces/ci.yml` at the frozen commit, parses it (a DEP-FREE parser — no js-yaml, which has no types + is a transitive-dep boot risk), creates the run + job rows, launches ONE job container via `launchTicketContainer` (same image/hardening/egress), runs each job's script via `docker exec` in stage order, records a `TicketEvent(type:'ci')` per job, and rolls up. No docker ⇒ `canceled` (never ran ⇒ does NOT gate red); no ci.yml ⇒ no run. 3. **The gate — default (A): gate + Admin override.** `ciGateForMr(mr, headSha)`: a red/running/stale run for the CURRENT head blocks the `mr-merge` op (a stale-

chunks.title: 0040-security-dependency-scanning
chunks.text: ADR 0040: 0040-security-dependency-scanning. C1 (ADR 0039) built the CI runner + the merge/promote gates. C2 adds the user's ask: security + dependency scanning built DIRECTLY into the pipeline (not only via automation/cron or manual tickets). It inherits C1's runner/DAG entirely — the job TYPES are the delta. Decision: 1. **First-class scanner job types on the C1 runner** — a CI job gains a `type` (`script` default, plus `dep-audit` / `sca` / `secret-scan`). A scanner job needs NO `script` (its command comes from its type: `npm audit --json` for dep-audit; a credential-pattern `grep` for secret-scan). Results are PARSED into typed findings + a max severity (`server/ci/security.ts` pure parsers), stored on the `PipelineJob` (`severity`, `findings`) and rolled up to `PipelineRun.maxSeverity` — not freeform log-grepping. 2. **Fail policy: high/critical blocks a PROD promote; report-only on dev/merge.** A scanner job stays green (it doesn't fail the run — so it never hard-blocks merge), but its SEVERITY is a separate prod gate: `securityBlocksProdPromote(projectId)` blocks `env-promote → prod` (`promote.securityFindings`) when the latest run carries a high/critical finding. This matches "build it into the pipeline" without making a moderate advisory wedge every merge.

chunks.title: 0041-ai-mr-review
chunks.text: ADR 0041: 0041-ai-mr-review. `BUILTIN_MR_REVIEW.md` designs an AI reviewer but marks it deferred, with a blanket "the AI never authors a review comment" posture. The SHIPPED schema, however, already widened `ReviewComment` for exactly this feature — `authorKind: 'user' | 'ai'` + optional `authorId`. C3 is the white-space item that fills it: an AI that reads an MR diff (RAG-grounded) and posts line-anchored findings — via propose→accept, never writing or approving directly. Decision: 1. **A non-coding `mr-review` AgentRole** (provider abstraction, ADR 0007 — new `AiFeature 'mr-review'`), mirroring the interviewer role. `run`: load the MR + `branchDiff` → `parseUnifiedDiff`, `retrieve()` the shared RAG for grounding, `runAiCompletion('mr-review', …)`, parse findings, and **validate every finding's line anchor against the real diff** (drop hallucinated line numbers). It emits ONE `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'mr-review')` carrying `{ mrId, findings[] }` in its `patch`. 2. **Propose→accept is the write boundary (B-23).** The AI NEVER writes a comment. On human accept, the `accept-suggestion` control-op dispatches a new `type === 'mr-review'` branch → the Conductor posts each finding as a real `ReviewComment(authorKind:'ai')` (no `authorId`). The AI never approves or merges — `mr-approve`/`mr-merge` stay human-only + approval-gated. This keeps the B-23 invariant intact at the write boundary while enabling an AI author on the comment. 3. **Reuses existing surfaces.** The proposal appe

chunks.title: 0042-ai-assisted-rollback
chunks.text: ADR 0042: 0042-ai-assisted-rollback. The forward-revert plumbing already exists (`mr-rollback` op → `rollbackMr` → `revertMergeCommit`, a history-preserving `git revert -m 1`, never a reset — invariant #7). The user wants an AI DRIVER on top: *"'X doet het niet meer' → AI figures out which changes likely caused it → rolls back → makes a ticket."* B3 adds that driver as a non-coding role, keeping the human in the loop for the actual revert (B-23). Decision: 1. **A non-coding `root-cause` AgentRole** (provider abstraction — new `AiFeature 'root-cause'`), mirroring the mr-review/interviewer roles. `run`: given a `symptom` + the recent merged MRs (newest first), `runAiCompletion('root-cause', …)` ranks the single most-likely culprit + explains why + what to verify. It parses `CULPRIT: <mr-number>` / `REASON: …` (pure `parseCulprit`), maps the number to the MR, and emits ONE `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'rollback', patch:{ mrId, symptom, reason })`. It NEVER reverts. 2. **Propose→accept is the write boundary (B-23).** On human accept, the `accept-suggestion` control-op dispatches a `type === 'rollback'` branch → `acceptRollback`: it runs the EXISTING `rollbackMr` (forward revert, invariant #7) on the ranked MR (best-effort — a no-op without a linked repo), then drafts a `DEV-####` tracking ticket pre-filled from the analysis (`labels:['rollback']`, high priority, the reason as the description, entering at `unrefined`), firing `ticket.created`. The AI never reverts directly; the Condu

chunks.title: 0043-user-app-db-migrations
chunks.text: ADR 0043: 0043-user-app-db-migrations. D1 gives a user's app a database surface: a read-only explorer + migration management. It ties to B1 environments (a migration targets an env's DB) and reuses the encrypted-secret path + the container/exec primitive. Greenfield — no DB model/op existed. Decision: 1. **`DbConnection` model** (per project, optionally per service/env; `kind` postgres/mysql/mongo; `urlEnc` ENCRYPTED via `secretBox`, never client-visible). The connection store the explorer + migrations resolve. 2. **Read-only explorer first (`introspectDb` / `db-introspect` op).** Lists a connection's tables/collections via a READ-ONLY listing query in a throwaway DB-client container (the base image has psql/mysql/mongosh). Browse-before-edit — the safest first cut. 3. **`Migration` model + gated apply (`db-migrate-apply` op).** A migration (`sql` + optional `rollbackSql`) is authored by the coding agent (schema-diff → SQL) and applied PER ENVIRONMENT as a control-op. Gates: **dev applies freely; prod requires an explicit approval AND a recorded rollback plan** (B-23 + the "prod apply = approval + backup/rollback" decision). Applied via the connection's DB client in a throwaway container; `status` tracks pending→applied/failed. The Conductor is the only applier (never client-side).

chunks.title: 0044-reasoning-plan-critique
chunks.text: ADR 0044: 0044-reasoning-plan-critique. E1 makes reasoning first-class: (1) a per-stage think-budget (reasoning effort / max-turns / auto-escalate) and (2) a plan-critique gate — an adversarial pass that attacks the plan before implement. Decision: 1. **Think-budget is ALREADY surfaced — no new work.** The per-stage `modelCfg` (`StageModelChoice`: `model`/`effort` low→max/`maxTurns` + `autoEscalate` + escalation `rules`) is editable in the pipeline page today (`src/workspaces/pipeline/page.tsx` — the effort `Segmented` + the turns input + the auto-escalate rules). E1 confirms this is the think-budget primitive; it needs no change. 2. **Plan-critique gate = a new adversarial role.** A non-coding `plan-critique` AgentRole (provider abstraction, `AiFeature 'plan-critique'`) reads a ticket's plan (the latest `CarryOver` envelope's `summary` + `openQuestions`) and attacks it — what's missing / what breaks / which assumption is risky — emitting a `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'plan-critique')` the human folds in before implement. It's read-only + advisory (no auto-apply); it runs through the suggestion/feed, **never a second AI window**. Triggered by a `plan-critique` control-op (a pipeline can call it after the plan stage, optional gate).

chunks.title: 0045-rag-institutional-memory
chunks.text: ADR 0045: 0045-rag-institutional-memory. The RAG index is already SINGULAR — one `RagEntry` store, one `retrieve()`, one embedder (`server/rag/{index,embed}.ts`). An earlier fix grounded the Workspace-AI chat. E2 finishes the wiring: consumption breadth + institutional memory, all on the same index (no parallel store). Decision: 1. **Institutional memory on the same store.** `server/rag/memory.ts` indexes the workspace's `Handoff` (summary/decisions/gotchas/next) + `CarryOver` (summary/open-questions) envelopes into `RagEntry` under a reserved sentinel commit `institutional-memory`. `retrieveMemory()` reuses the single `retrieve()` with that sentinel — so prior learnings surface via the SAME retrieval path, no second index. Frozen- per-"commit" replace (mirrors code indexing). Un-defers `additions/03_institutional_memory`. 2. **Incremental re-index on merge.** A successful `mr-merge` fires a best-effort re-index of the code RAG (the target branch advanced) + the institutional memory — off the caller's path, never blocking the merge. Previously re-index was manual-only ("Reindex code"). 3. **Wire retrieval into more surfaces.** The plan-critique role (E1) now grounds its critique in `retrieveMemory()` — repeated past mistakes become the highest-value gaps. (The C3 mr-review role already grounds on `retrieve()`.) An `index-memory` control-op (re)builds the memory on demand.

chunks.title: 0046-greenfield-scaffolding
chunks.text: ADR 0046: 0046-greenfield-scaffolding. F1 adds "create a NEW project from a stack template" — the GENERATE side of the GENERATE-vs-LINK split (features/01). `additions/04` covers onboarding an EXISTING repo; F1 covers a fresh one, plus a welcome flow. It builds on A1's multi-project model (a template creates a project) + the project-create/default- pipeline path. Decision: 1. **A small CURATED template catalog** (`server/scaffold/templates.ts`) — a few reviewed stacks (node-api, react-vite, python-fastapi), each carrying the seed config a fresh project needs: a base image hint, a dev command, and starter convention docs. Pure data + `listTemplates()`/`getTemplate()`. A cross-workspace template marketplace is later (features/01 B-O4). 2. **`project-from-template` control-op** — creates a fresh `Project` (reusing the A1 project model) with the template's `devCommand`/`baseImageRef`, seeds the template's starter convention docs as `InfoSource(source:'starter')` (visible in Sources, injectable into the coding agent — the starter-doc pattern), and seeds the project's own default pipeline (`createDefaultPipeline`). The catalog is exposed in the snapshot (`templates[]`) for the picker. 3. **Welcome flow — the data + method are wired; the wizard UI is a follow-up.** `templates` + `createFromTemplate` are on the context; a first-run wizard on top of the existing setup steps is the remaining UX layer (a picker rendering `templates[]` → `createFromTemplate`).

chunks.title: 0047-delivery-analytics
chunks.text: ADR 0047: 0047-delivery-analytics. G1 un-defers PRODUCT_ANALYTICS: cycle-time, throughput, stuck-points, and token-cost-by-type, folded over the append-only `TicketEvent` + `SpendRecord`/usage log. The `computeInsights` fold already exists (avgCycle/throughput/avgTokens); G1 adds the fuller analytics + a dashboard surface. Cost in TOKENS, not € (invariant #9 — the parked price-blocking). Decision: 1. **A PURE on-request fold — no new write path/model/verb** (`server/obs/analytics.ts` `computeAnalytics`). It folds tickets + the already-aggregated usage into: cycle-time **p50/p85** (p85 = the robust "how long does it really take", not a mean skewed by outliers), **weekly throughput** (4 buckets), **stuck-points** (tickets parked in stuck/paused/needs-input), and **token cost by label** (cost per work TYPE). `now` is injected → deterministic + unit-testable. Advisory — it gates nothing. 2. **Surfaced on the Usage page** — the snapshot emits `analytics` (alongside the existing `insights`); the Usage page renders a "Delivery analytics" card (p85/stuck/weekly stat cards + a throughput bar chart + a tokens-by-type list). No new page/route.

chunks.title: 0048-review-ergonomics
chunks.text: ADR 0048: 0048-review-ergonomics. G2 un-defers additions/05 + 06: a cross-ticket **answer-queue** (drain every pending question from one place, phone-first) + **presence/claim** (who's viewing/answering + a soft-claim so two reviewers don't double-answer). The presence relay already exists (`_sync/presence`, ephemeral who's-viewing). Decision: 1. **Answer-queue = a snapshot-derived cross-ticket view.** Every ticket parked on a question (`Ticket.needsInput` set, or status `needs-input`) surfaces in `snapshot.answerQueue` (`ticketKey`, `title`, `question`, `priority`), highest-priority first — one queue the reviewer swipes/stacks through instead of hunting per-ticket. Pure derivation over the existing tickets — no new write path/model. 2. **Soft-claim on the presence relay.** The presence event gains a `claiming` flag: a reviewer answering a ticket broadcasts `{viewing:true, claiming:true}`; the client renders "X is answering" and can disable the answer input for others. Ephemeral + idempotent (like viewing) — the authenticated user id comes from the session (unspoofable), the socket room fan-out makes it multi-instance-safe for free. NOT authoritative state (no Conductor write) — it's a coordination hint, not a lock.

chunks.title: 0049-content-platform-pivot
chunks.text: ADR 0049: 0049-content-platform-pivot. Workspaces began as an AI **dev-orchestration** environment (tickets → pipeline → coding agent, human-in-the-middle). With the Studio marketing module (ADR 0033) it became clear the product is really an **all-in-1 tool for using AI in many ways**. The user wants to add AI **content creation** as a first-class use: short + long-form video, reference-driven photorealistic imagery, avatars, music, 3D, auto-posting to platforms, and animated software demos — driven by the same "user approves, the engine executes" model. This is a deliberate scope expansion the user wants; the question was whether it fits the architecture. It does — as an **addition, not a rewrite**. Decision: **Add a content lane on the existing engine.** A `projectType` (`dev` | `content` | …) selects the workflow lane; the same Conductor, realtime, RBAC, RAG, cron/automation, control-ops and B-23 single-writer serve both. Content is NOT a separate product — one app, distinct workflow surfaces. Concretely: 1. **The pipeline engine is generic.** A content-pipeline (idea → script → generate → assemble → review → publish) is just different stage-configs + roles on the same stage-runner. 2. **The provider abstraction (ADR 0007) is the "one tool for everything"** — our tool is the router, not a single external vendor. Default gateway **Fal.ai** (image/video/3d) + **ElevenLabs** (voice) + **Remotion** (code-driven assembly) + **Gemini** (reference/video analysis); per-workspace p

chunks.title: 0050-content-data-model
chunks.text: ADR 0050: 0050-content-data-model. First item of `CONTENT_PLATFORM_PROGRAM.md` (ADR 0049) — schema-first. The content lane needs its data model published before any engine/client work. Decision: 1. **A `projectType` on Project** (`'dev'` | `'content'`, default `'dev'`) selects the workflow lane. Zero migration for existing projects (default). 2. **Nine content models**, all tenant-scoped by **explicit `workspaceId` filtering** (NOT the `tenantDb` `$extends` auto-scoping): `Channel` (distribution target + house style), `ContentProject` (a content piece flowing the pipeline — `stageId`/`status` mirror Ticket so the generic stage-runner drives it), `ContentAsset` (a produced media asset), `Script` + `Beat` (narration + storyboard), `MediaJob` (async generation to a provider, `costCents` metered), `RenderJob` (Remotion assembly), `StylePreset` (a named style, `workspaceId` null = global default / set = per-workspace), `MediaSpend` (the €-cost ledger, cents). 3. **Media cost in CENTS** on `MediaJob`/`RenderJob`/`MediaSpend` — metered real-money €, distinct from the coding-agent token accounting (invariant #9).

chunks.title: 0051-media-budget-guard
chunks.text: ADR 0051: 0051-media-budget-guard. Media APIs (Fal/Veo/ElevenLabs/3d) are **metered real-money** per generation — unlike the coding agent, which runs on the Max subscription and is accounted in tokens (invariant #9). A cron-driven content loop could run up a real bill, so a per-workspace **€-cap + pre-generation guard** is needed before any generation lands. Decision: 1. **A `MediaBudget` model** — ONE row per workspace (`@@unique workspaceId`), `capCents`/`spentCents`/`alertPct`/`enabled`, opt-in (disabled by default). Cents (Int) — no float money. 2. **A pure guard `checkMediaBudget(prisma, ws, costCents)`** (`server/media/budget.ts`) → `{ ok, reason?, unlimited, capCents, spentCents, remainingCents }`. No budget / `!enabled` / `capCents<=0` = **unlimited** (always ok). Over cap → `ok:false, reason:'media.budgetExceeded'`. Pure read; the caller records on success. `recordMediaSpend(...)` writes the `MediaSpend` €-ledger row + debits `spentCents`. `getMediaBudgetStatus(...)` exposes the status (incl. `overAlert`) for the settings UI + snapshot. 3. **The budget is set via an `edit-media-budget` control-op** (B-23 write path) — capability `workspaceSettings`, Conductor upserts the row. The user never writes the budget directly.

chunks.title: 0052-media-provider-abstraction
chunks.text: ADR 0052: 0052-media-provider-abstraction. The content lane generates ASSETS (images/video/voice/…), not text. The existing AI-provider abstraction (ADR 0007, `server/ai/*`) is text-completion-shaped (`AiCompletionResult.text`). Media needs the same *pattern* (features resolve to a provider; no feature hardcodes a backend) but a different *result shape* (an asset + a metered € cost). No API keys exist yet — the whole pipeline must run on dummy data. Decision: 1. **A parallel MEDIA layer** in `server/media/` mirroring `server/ai/`: `MediaFeature` (`image-gen`, `reference-image`, `video-gen`, `tts`, `music`, `sfx`, `avatar`, `model-3d`), `MediaProviderId` (`fal`, `elevenlabs`), `MediaGenerationRequest`/`Result` (asset + `costCents` + `stub` flag), `MediaProvider` interface, `DEFAULT_MEDIA_ASSIGNMENTS` + `resolveMediaAssignment` (per-workspace override seam), and `runMediaGeneration(req, overrides)` dispatch. 2. **Registry-level STUB fallback.** Each adapter's `available()` is false until its key env is present; when unavailable, `runMediaGeneration` returns a valid-SHAPED stub asset (`stub://<kind>/<feature>/<style>`) + a realistic declared `costCents` (video » image » voice). So the entire content pipeline runs end-to-end on dummy data, and the €-budget guard (F0.2) is exercised — without any keys. 3. **`reference-video-analysis` stays a TEXT `AiFeature`** on `gemini-api` (extends `server/ai` union + `DEFAULT_ASSIGNMENTS`) — it returns a beat/style BLUEPRINT (text/structured),

chunks.title: 0053-style-preset-system
chunks.text: ADR 0053: 0053-style-preset-system. ADR 0049 makes styles a first-class, cross-cutting concept: every AI feature (text or media) composes a generation from `feature + input + style + free-form extra instructions`. A style is a curated system-prompt preset (e.g. `realistisch`, `cinematic`), with global defaults + per-workspace (brand) overrides. The `StylePreset` model exists (F0.1); F0.4 builds the resolve/compose/seed logic + the write path. Decision: 1. **`server/content/styles.ts`** — `ensureDefaultStyles` (idempotent seed of the global `builtin` styles, `workspaceId=null`), `resolveStyle(prisma, ws, feature, key)` (a per-workspace style with the same key WINS over the global; no key/no match → null), `composeStylePrompt(style, extra)` (style system-prompt + free-form extra instructions, joined), and `listStyles` (global + workspace, the workspace shadowing the global — for the picker UI). 2. **Per-workspace styles are written via a `save-style` control-op** (B-23; capability `workspaceSettings`; Conductor upserts by `(workspace, feature, key)`). Global styles are seed-only (`builtin`, not user-writable). 3. **Styles thread into gen at the CALL SITE, not into `runAiCompletion`'s signature.** The content pipeline (F1.x) resolves the style + composes the system prompt, then passes it as `req.system` (text) or `MediaGenerationRequest.style` (media). No feature signature changes.

chunks.title: 0054-content-pipeline
chunks.text: ADR 0054: 0054-content-pipeline. A content piece (`ContentProject`) must flow through a workflow the way a Ticket flows through the dev board. F1.1 builds that engine: the stage sequence + the control-ops that drive a piece through it (the per-stage generation wires in F1.2–F1.5). Decision: 1. **A FIXED ordered content-stage sequence** (`server/content/pipeline.ts`): `idea → script → generate → assemble → review → publish`, with `nextContentStage`/`isContentStage` helpers. Unlike the dev board (per-project `PipelineStage` rows), the content stages are a code constant — the sequence is uniform across content pieces (per-stage CONFIG comes later, F4). 2. **Three control-ops** (B-23; capability `workTickets`): `content-create` (make a `ContentProject` at `idea`), `content-advance` (→ an explicit `toStage`, else the next stage; past `publish` → `status:done`), `content-archive` (soft). The **Conductor is the only writer** of `stageId`/`status`. 3. **`project-create` gains `projectType`** — `projectType:'content'` makes a content-lane project (NO board pipeline seeded); default stays `dev` (a board + its `PipelineStage`s). Zero change for existing dev flows.

chunks.title: 0055-content-script-generation
chunks.text: ADR 0055: 0055-content-script-generation. The `script` stage turns a brief into a narration Script + storyboard Beats (each beat carries a `visualPrompt` that drives the per-beat image in F1.4). Script generation is text, so it uses the text AI abstraction (`runAiCompletion`) — but that has NO stub fallback (unlike the media registry, F0.3), and no keys exist. So with no key it would return `ai.providerUnavailable` and the pipeline would stall. Decision: 1. **A content-script service `server/content/script.ts`** — `generateScript(prisma, { workspaceId, contentProjectId, brief, styleKey?, extraInstructions? })` resolves the `script` style + composes the system prompt (F0.4), calls `runAiCompletion('script', …)`, then writes a `Script` + ordered `Beat` rows and returns `{ scriptId, beatCount, stub, providerId }`. 2. **A CONTENT-LOCAL stub fallback.** When the provider is unavailable (no key), `generateScript` produces a valid-shaped 4-beat script from the brief (dummy-data mode) — the stub lives in the content layer, NOT in `runAiCompletion`, so the global text abstraction (incl. the coding agent) never silently stubs. 3. **`script` is a text `AiFeature`** (default `gemini-api` — non-coding bulk text, overridable). The `Script` records the resolved `providerId` + links the resolved `styleId`. 4. **Driven by a `content-gen-script` control-op** (B-23, `workTickets`) — the Conductor calls `generateScript` for the piece.

chunks.title: 0056-content-voiceover
chunks.text: ADR 0056: 0056-content-voiceover. The `generate` stage turns a Script into a voice asset. This is the first item to run the FULL metered media path end-to-end (budget-check → media gen → asset + spend), and it must produce the per-beat timing the montage (F1.5) needs to align visuals to the narration. Decision: 1. **`server/content/voice.ts` `generateVoiceover`** runs the whole path: `estimateMediaCostCents('tts')` → `checkMediaBudget` (block BEFORE the paid call) → `runMediaGeneration({feature:'tts', …})` (stub when no key) → a voice `ContentAsset` + a `MediaJob` (linked `resultAssetId`) → `recordMediaSpend`. Returns `{ ok, blocked?, assetId, costCents, stub, totalMs }`. 2. **Budget-check BEFORE gen, via `estimateMediaCostCents`** — a new registry export returning the expected cost so the guard runs before the (paid) call; the actual `result.costCents` is recorded after. A cap hit returns `blocked:true` and runs no gen. 3. **Per-beat timing** — each `Beat` gets a persisted `durationMs` (word-count-derived, min 1.5s), and the voice asset's `metadata` carries `{ totalMs, timing[] }` (cumulative start + duration per beat). Deterministic → testable.

chunks.title: 0057-content-beat-images
chunks.text: ADR 0057: 0057-content-beat-images. Each storyboard `Beat` needs a visual for the montage. F1.4 generates one image per beat via `image-gen` (stub, no key), in the chosen style + extra instructions, and links it on the beat. Decision: `server/content/images.ts` `generateBeatImages` loops the script's beats: per beat it budget-checks (`estimateMediaCostCents('image-gen')` → `checkMediaBudget`), runs `runMediaGeneration({feature:'image-gen', prompt: beat.visualPrompt})`, writes a `MediaJob` + an image `ContentAsset`, links `Beat.imageAssetId`, and records the spend. It **stops early (partial result) if the budget cap is hit** mid-loop. Driven by the `content-gen-images` control-op (B-23, `workTickets`).

chunks.title: 0058-content-assembly
chunks.text: ADR 0058: 0058-content-assembly. The final `assemble` stage composes a piece's beats (+ their images) + the voiceover into the COMPLETE downloadable output. This closes Fase 1 — the content pipeline produces a finished asset end-to-end. No keys, so the render is a stub; the render itself is Remotion (local CPU), not a metered API. Decision: 1. **`server/content/assembly.ts` `assembleContent`** builds a Remotion timeline (`{ order, text, imageAssetId, durationMs }` per beat, over the voice asset, `totalMs` summed), writes a `RenderJob` (`composition:'faceless'`, `status:'done'`), and produces the final `ContentAsset` (`kind:'render'`, `metadata.downloadable=true` + `hasVoice`/`hasAllImages`/`beatCount`/`totalMs`), linking `RenderJob.resultAssetId`. 2. **Local render is FREE (`costCents:0`)** — Remotion renders on CPU, not a metered media API, so it does NOT debit the €-budget (only the gen calls do: voice + images). This keeps the cost model honest. 3. **The render asset IS the deliverable** — its `stub://render/<piece>` url + `downloadable` flag is the complete output the user downloads + posts manually (the primary near-term path). A real HTTP download route is F3.3. 4. Driven by the `content-assemble` control-op (B-23, `workTickets`).

chunks.title: 0059-reference-image
chunks.text: ADR 0059: 0059-reference-image. The user's #1-priority feature: generate an image CONDITIONED on a reference image, in a chosen style (realism first) + free-form extra instructions (e.g. "dancing, brown curly hair"). The `reference-image` media feature exists (F0.3); F2.1 wires the content-side flow. Decision: `server/content/referenceImage.ts` `generateReferenceImage` runs the metered path: `checkMediaBudget('reference-image')` → `runMediaGeneration({feature:'reference-image', referenceUrl, style, extraInstructions})` (stub) → an image `ContentAsset` (`metadata.hasReference`) + a `MediaJob` (records the `referenceUrl` + `styleId`) → `recordMediaSpend`. **The style defaults to `realistisch`** unless overridden (realism is the priority). Driven by the `content-gen-reference-image` op (B-23, `workTickets`), which requires a `referenceUrl`.

chunks.title: 0060-short-form-clips
chunks.text: ADR 0060: 0060-short-form-clips. A short-form (TikTok/Shorts/Reels) clip is a single hook-driven vertical video, distinct from the assembled faceless-explainer. F2.2 generates it via `video-gen` (stub) with a hook + captions. Decision: `server/content/shortForm.ts` `generateShortForm` runs the metered path (`checkMediaBudget('video-gen')` → `runMediaGeneration({feature:'video-gen'})` stub → video `ContentAsset` + `MediaJob` + spend), derives a `hook` + `captions` from the prompt (stub; a live hook-writer lands with keys), and stores them on the asset metadata (`format:'short'`). Driven by `content-gen-shortform` (B-23, `workTickets`, requires a `prompt`).

chunks.title: 0061-reference-video-analysis
chunks.text: ADR 0061: 0061-reference-video-analysis. The user wants to "mimic another video's storytelling/pacing/style over a NEW story". F2.3 analyses a reference video (multimodal, Gemini) into a beat/style BLUEPRINT and retells a new story in that shape. Decision: `server/content/referenceVideo.ts` `analyzeReferenceVideo` calls the `reference-video-analysis` text AiFeature (Gemini, video-capable), producing a `VideoBlueprint` (`pacing`, `styleHint`, `beats[]`), then SEEDS a `Script` (title "From reference video") + `Beat`s from it — the NEW story in the reference's shape. Content-local stub (no key). Driven by `content-analyze-reference-video` (B-23, `workTickets`, requires `referenceVideoUrl` + `newStory`).

chunks.title: 0062-media-asset-avatar
chunks.text: ADR 0062: 0062-media-asset-avatar. Avatar/music/sfx/3d are simple "prompt (+ style) → one asset" gens with identical plumbing (budget → gen → asset → spend). F2.4 builds the shared helper + wires avatar; F2.5/F2.6 reuse it. Decision: `server/content/mediaAsset.ts` `generateMediaAsset(prisma, { feature, prompt?, referenceUrl?, styleKey?, extraInstructions? })` is the generic metered path for the simple single-asset features. The 4 ops (`content-gen-avatar`/`-music`/`-sfx`/`-3d`, B-23, `workTickets`) share ONE Conductor case that maps op→`MediaFeature` and calls it. The specialised services (voice timing, per-beat images, short-form captions, reference-image) keep their own files.

chunks.title: 0063-music-sfx
chunks.text: ADR 0063: 0063-music-sfx. The montage benefits from a soundtrack + sound effects. F2.5 adds music + sfx gen — both simple single-asset gens, so they reuse the shared `generateMediaAsset` path (F2.4). Decision: Music + sfx generation ride the `content-gen-music` / `content-gen-sfx` ops (already wired in F2.4's shared Conductor case → `generateMediaAsset` with feature `music`/`sfx`). Both default to the ElevenLabs adapter (stub, no key). Music (Suno) gets a dedicated provider later; for now it routes to the voice adapter's stub.

chunks.title: 0064-model-3d
chunks.text: ADR 0064: 0064-model-3d. 3D is the weakest modality (concepting-grade, not hero assets) + lowest priority (ADR 0049). F2.6 adds it as a simple single-asset gen on the shared path — closing Fase 2 (all modalities present). Decision: 3D generation rides the `content-gen-3d` op (wired in F2.4's shared Conductor case → `generateMediaAsset` with feature `model-3d`, default fal/Meshy-class provider, stub). No new engine code.

chunks.title: 0065-publish-gate
chunks.text: ADR 0065: 0065-publish-gate. Posting to a real channel is irreversible + public — the exact case B-23 reserves for an explicit human confirm. F3.1 builds publishing behind that gate, with a platform-adapter abstraction + a YouTube adapter (dummy, no key). Decision: 1. **`content-request-publish` creates a publish SUGGESTION** (`WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'publish', patch:{contentProjectId, assetId, platform})`) — it does NOT post. Accepting it (`accept-suggestion` → the new `'publish'` branch) makes the **Conductor** call `publishAsset` (the only writer of the `PublishJob`). The AI never publishes. 2. **A platform abstraction** (`server/content/publish.ts`) with `BUILT_PLATFORMS` (youtube, tiktok) + `FUTURE_PLATFORMS` (instagram, linkedin). A built platform with no key → a **dummy post** returning a `stub://<platform>/<asset>` external url; a future-ready platform → a `PublishJob(status:error, error:'platform.notBuilt')` (recorded, not posted). 3. **A `PublishJob` model** records each post (platform, status, externalUrl, error).

chunks.title: 0066-publish-tiktok
chunks.text: ADR 0066: 0066-publish-tiktok. F3.2 adds TikTok posting (same B-23 gate) + registers Instagram/LinkedIn as future-ready (not built now). Decision: TikTok is in `BUILT_PLATFORMS` (established in F3.1's abstraction) — it posts via the same gate + `publishAsset` (dummy, no key). Instagram + LinkedIn stay in `FUTURE_PLATFORMS`: a publish request for them records a `PublishJob(error:'platform.notBuilt')` — visible, never a silent post. No new engine code beyond F3.1's abstraction.

chunks.title: 0067-content-automation
chunks.text: ADR 0067: 0067-content-automation. Two entry modes for content (ADR 0049): recurring channel automation (cron) + a conversational quick-start (the Assistant spins up a piece from a brief). F3.3 wires both, reusing the automation engine (ADR 0027) + the content pipeline (F1.1). Decision: 1. **A schedulable `content-ideator` AgentRole** (`server/content/ideatorRole.ts`, `mutates:true`). A cron trigger (`action:'invoke-agent-role', params:{role:'content-ideator', theme?}`) fires it; because it `mutates`, the automation executor GATES it into an approval suggestion — it never writes content directly (B-23). Registered at boot in `server.ts`. 2. **A `content-from-brief` op** (B-23, `workTickets`) — the conversational quick-start: creates a content-lane `Project` + a first `ContentProject` piece from a chat brief in one op (on the user's accept). This is what the Assistant calls to "spin up a video about startup A".

chunks.title: 0068-nav-grouping
chunks.text: ADR 0068: 0068-nav-grouping. The main nav rail is a flat list of 11 items — the user asked to declutter it with better GROUPING + a contextual secondary navbar, plus lazy-loading for bundle size. F4.1 delivers the grouping (the highest-value, lowest-risk part) now; the richer per-area secondary navbar + lazy-loading are scoped follow-ups (they need browser verification, which is deferred with no keys/running server). Decision: Each `NavDef` gets a `group` (`work` | `build` | `studio` | `insights`); the rail renders items grouped under section headers (expanded) or thin dividers (collapsed), in `GROUP_ORDER`. Group labels render via a variable (`GROUP_LABELS[g]`), matching the existing nav's variable-rendered `it.label` (no new i18n debt; consistent with the current pattern). Theme tokens only (`text-disabled`, `bg-divider`).

chunks.title: 0069-content-snapshot-ui
chunks.text: ADR 0069: 0069-content-snapshot-ui. The content UI + settings need the content state on the client. F4.2 wires the content lane into the workspace snapshot (the testable, enabling core); the rich page components + the settings FORM are the browser-deferred layer (no keys / running server for a visual pass). Decision: The snapshot gains `content: ContentSnapshot` — `pieces` (the non-archived `ContentProject`s: id/title/format/stageId/status/channelId) + `mediaBudget` (the `getMediaBudgetStatus` fold: enabled/cap/spent/alert/overAlert). Content models scope by explicit `workspaceId` (via `currentWorkspaceId()` inside `runInTenant`), matching the feature-model pattern (ADR 0050) — NOT `tenantDb` (content isn't in `TENANT_MODELS`). Threaded through `WorkspacesProvider` + `WorkspacesContext` so any content surface reads `content` from context.

chunks.title: 0070-copilot
chunks.text: ADR 0070: 0070-copilot. The user wants the AI to steer the app (navigate + pre-fill forms) for a good UX — but B-23 forbids LLMs writing authoritative state, and literal pixel-clicking of our own UI is an anti-pattern (ADR 0049). F4.3 builds the copilot as a PROPOSAL model: the Assistant proposes a UI directive; the client applies the navigate/pre-fill guidance; the user confirms the underlying control-op (the Conductor writes). Decision: A `copilot-propose` op (B-23, `workTickets`) creates a `WorkspaceSuggestion(type:'copilot', patch:{navigate, prefill, op})` — the UI directive: WHERE to navigate, WHAT to pre-fill a form with, and the underlying control-op the user would confirm. The copilot **writes nothing authoritative** — only the proposal. The client (browser-deferred) reads it, navigates + pre-fills, and the user taps the real control-op (which the Conductor executes). This is "AI drives, human confirms".

chunks.title: 0071-content-memory-analytics
chunks.text: ADR 0071: 0071-content-memory-analytics. The final item: a per-channel brand/style memory (so a channel's generations stay on-brand) + a content-analytics fold (what ships, where pieces sit, the metered cost). Decision: 1. **Per-channel brand memory** (`server/content/brandMemory.ts`) reuses the SINGLE unified RAG store + `retrieve()` under a per-channel sentinel commit `brand:<channelId>` (mirrors the institutional-memory sentinel, ADR 0045). `indexChannelBrand` (re-)indexes a channel's brand snippets; `retrieveChannelBrand` retrieves them for that channel only — no parallel index, no cross-channel leakage. 2. **A PURE content-analytics fold** (`server/content/contentAnalytics.ts` `computeContentAnalytics`) over pieces + media spend + publish jobs → `totalPieces`, `doneCount`, `publishedCount`, `byStage`, `byFormat`, `totalCostCents`, `costByFeature`. Deterministic → testable; views/CTR are placeholders until platform keys land.

chunks.title: 0072-depth-program
chunks.text: ADR 0072: 0072-depth-program. A 3-agent depth audit (`src/workspaces/_docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md`) found: the code/dev-orchestration side + the contract spine are genuinely deep + real, but (a) the content platform is a hollow stub skeleton — no real generation/render/publish code (the live `generate()` returns `notImplemented`) and NO user-facing UI at all (unreachable; the `snapshot.content` is dead state), and (b) three cross-cutting depth risks: a tenant-isolation leak surface (new + content models are outside `tenantDb`'s loud-fail guarantee), encryption that fails OPEN (`secretBox` → `plain:` when `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` is unset), and ~0% real-infra test coverage. The user wants a real, usable product, not a half-fake one. Decision: Run a `DEPTH_PROGRAM.md` `/goal` build (16 items, H→C→M→U→D) that: 1. **Hardens the platform first** — fold every `workspaceId` model into the tenant isolation guarantee (or lint it) so it can never leak; hard-force `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` (fail-closed). 2. **Fixes the code-side edges** — MR merge/rollback push-to-origin, container readiness probes (no fire-and-forget), retry/backoff + pagination, a real CI-YAML parser + PTY prompt-ready detection. (Docker-dependency is ACCEPTED — no fix.) 3. **Writes the REAL content code behind every `available()` gate** — real Fal/Replicate + ElevenLabs + Suno + Gemini generation, a real ffmpeg (Docker) render pipeline, real YouTube/TikTok OAuth + upload. The stub becomes PURELY the no-key fallback. 4. **Builds the

chunks.title: 0073-tenant-scope-lint-guard
chunks.text: ADR 0073: 0073-tenant-scope-lint-guard. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` cross-cutting #1: `tenantDb`'s loud-fail row-isolation covers only the ~24 core `TENANT_MODELS`. Every newer model (Service/Forge/Environment/CI/Deploy + the ENTIRE content set — 55 models carry `workspaceId`) lives OUTSIDE that guarantee and relies on hand-written `workspaceId` filters on a plain `prisma` client. One forgotten filter = a silent cross-tenant leak; one already existed (`environment.findMany({ status:'live' })`, unscoped). `DEPTH_PROGRAM.md` H1 offered two branches: (a) fold every `workspaceId` model into `tenantDb`'s `TENANT_MODELS`, OR (b) an `ai:lint` rule that forbids a plain-`prisma` read/write on a `workspaceId` model. Decision: Chose branch (b) — a new diff-scoped `tenant-scope` `ai:lint` rule — plus fixing the one known unscoped call. - **The rule:** in `server/**` code, a `prisma.<model>.<read|write>(…)` on any of the 55 `workspaceId`-carrying models that does NOT constrain by `workspaceId` on the call line is a finding. `tenantDb.*` is exempt (it keys off the literal `prisma.` receiver). A deliberate cross-tenant sweep documents itself with `// luckystack-allow tenant-scope: <why>`. - **The known leak:** `reassertEnvironmentRoutes`'s `environment.findMany` is a leader-gated boot self-heal that MUST see every workspace's live envs — marked with the allow-comment (it is a correct cross-tenant sweep, not a leak). - **Verify:** six selftest cases (`npm run ai:lint -- --selftest`, 22/22) assert the

chunks.title: 0074-encryption-fail-closed
chunks.text: ADR 0074: 0074-encryption-fail-closed. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` cross-cutting #2: `secretBox` silently fell back to storing `plain:<base64>` (UNENCRYPTED) when `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` was unset, with only a one-time console warning. A `plain:` credential in production is unacceptable — the per-workspace GitLab/GitHub token, DB-connection URLs, and the editor profile blob would land at rest as recoverable plaintext. Decision: Make at-rest encryption **fail-closed**: - `encryptSecret` and `encryptBuffer` now **THROW** a clear error when no key is configured — they never emit a `plain:`/`0x00` plaintext envelope again. - New `assertEncryptionConfigured()` is called at **boot** (in `server.ts`, right after the secret-manager resolves) so the server refuses to start into a state where a stored secret would be plaintext — a loud fatal, not a lazy surprise. - `encryptionConfigured()` is exported for precondition checks. - **Migration path preserved:** `decryptSecret`/`decryptBuffer` STILL read any LEGACY `plain:`/`0x00` values written before this change, so pre-hardening dev data stays readable (re-save such secrets to encrypt them at rest). This closes the fail-OPEN *write* — the actual gap — without silently losing existing data. - **Tests:** `tests/unit/secretBox.test.mts` (14/14) asserts round-trip with a key, tamper→null, encrypt/assert THROW without a key, never-plain:, and legacy decrypt. The test harness (`tests/_helpers.mts`) sets a deterministic `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` after secret res

chunks.title: 0075-mr-push-to-origin
chunks.text: ADR 0075: 0075-mr-push-to-origin. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` code-side #1: `mergeBranches`/`revertMergeCommit` advance the `target` branch IN THE LOCAL BARE CLONE, but nothing pushed the result to origin — `pushBranch` existed yet was never called on the merge/rollback path. So a "merged" MR never actually reached the forge ref. Decision: - New `pushRef(workspaceId, gitUrl, token, ref)` in `repoStore` pushes a branch straight from the BARE clone to origin (the merge/revert advance `target` there). Token injected transiently via `withAuth`, never stored/logged.
