Bounded **retry/backoff** via a new shared `withRetry` helper (`server/util/retry.ts`, reused by C3). - New `pushMergedTarget(prisma, workspaceId, ticketId, targetBranch)` in `forge.ts` resolves the ticket's `project.gitUrl` + the per-project forge token (`resolveForge`) and pushes the target. **Non-fatal:** the local merge is authoritative; a `local-only` project (no gitUrl/token) is a SKIP, and a push failure is surfaced (`pushError`), never rolled back. - Wired into `mergeMr` (after a successful merge) and `rollbackMr` (after a successful revert); `MergeMrResult` gains `pushed?`/`pushError?` so the client/log can see whether the forge received it.

chunks.title: 0076-container-readiness-probes
chunks.text: ADR 0076: 0076-container-readiness-probes. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` code-side #3: the preview + editor flows dispatch a serve-command with `docker exec -d` (detached) and immediately flip the reverse-proxy route + return a URL — assuming success. A real `health.waitForContainerReady` probe existed but was only called by the deploy path (`environment.ts`). So a user opening a preview/editor got a URL that 502s until the dev-server / openvscode-server finished booting (10–30s). Decision: - Parametrized `waitForContainerReady(containerName, port, opts)` — `opts` = `{ attempts, delayMs, acceptAnyStatus, run }`. `acceptAnyStatus` drops curl's `-f` so a token-gated `401` (openvscode's root before the connection-token) still counts as bound; `run` is an injectable probe runner so the retry loop is unit-testable without Docker. - `openPreviewForTicket` now probes `PREVIEW_PORT` after starting the dev server and returns `preview.notReady` on timeout INSTEAD of flipping the route to a dead URL. - `openEditorForTicket` now probes `EDITOR_IN_CONTAINER_PORT` (with `acceptAnyStatus`) after `startEditorInContainer` and returns `editor.notReady` on timeout before flipping the route. - The deploy path (`environment.ts`) already called the probe — unchanged (the new default `opts` is backward-compatible).

chunks.title: 0077-forge-retry-pagination
chunks.text: ADR 0077: 0077-forge-retry-pagination. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` code-side #4: `fetchGitlabIssues`/`fetchGithubIssues` fetched a single `per_page=100` page — a project with >100 open issues silently lost the rest. Network ops had no retry/backoff (a transient blip dropped a git push or a sync). Decision: - **Pagination:** a pure `accumulatePages(fetchPage, {perPage, maxPages})` follows `page=1..` until a short page or a safety cap (`MAX_ISSUE_PAGES=20` → 2000 issues). Hitting the cap sets `capped` and the caller `console.warn`s it — **never a silent truncation**. Both GitLab + GitHub sync use it. - **Retry:** each page fetch + `pushBranch` (push-on-approval) run through `withRetry` (ADR 0075). `isTransientForgeError` retries only 5xx/429/network — a 4xx (bad token / not-found) fails fast. - Both helpers exported for a network-free unit test.

chunks.title: 0078-real-ci-yaml-pty-ready
chunks.text: ADR 0078: 0078-real-ci-yaml-pty-ready. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` code-side #5: (a) the CI parser was a fixed-indent mini-subset (2-space job names, 4-space fields, inline arrays only) — a real `.gitlab-ci.yml` (top-level jobs, `stages:`/`script:` as block sequences) was largely dropped; (b) the interactive `claude` turn used hardcoded `wait(7000)`/`wait(3000)` before confirming folder-trust + sending the kickoff — fragile on a slow boot, wasteful on a fast one. Decision: - **Real YAML:** a dep-free recursive YAML-subset parser (`parseYamlSubset`) handles block mappings at any consistent indent, block sequences (`- item`), inline flow arrays, quoted scalars, and comments. `parseCiYaml` reads it into the same `CiSpec`, accepting BOTH the documented `jobs:`-wrapped shape (backward compatible) AND a real `.gitlab-ci.yml` (top-level jobs, reserved keys like `variables:` skipped, snake_case `allow_failure`). Still no js-yaml (a transitive dep is a boot-crash risk) and still pure + total (a bad config → `{ok:false}`, never throws). - **PTY prompt-ready:** `server/orchestrator/ptyReady.ts` scans the accumulated PTY output for the CLI's trust/ready markers; `waitForOutput` early-exits as soon as one appears, with a ceiling so a wrong/missing marker DEGRADES to a bounded wait (never a hang, never worse than the old fixed wait). `stageRunner` accumulates `term.onData` and gates the trust-confirm + kickoff on detection.

chunks.title: 0079-real-fal-media-gen
chunks.text: ADR 0079: 0079-real-fal-media-gen. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #2: the Fal provider's `generate()` returned `media.notImplemented` — the whole image/video/3d/reference-image surface was fake `stub://`. The user clarified: fake CODE was never asked for (only fake TESTS for the no-key rounds). This item writes the REAL fal.ai code behind `available()`, keeping the stub as the pure no-key fallback. Decision: - `server/media/providers/fal.ts` now has a LIVE `generate()`: it composes the prompt (style system-prompt + prompt + extra instructions, ADR 0053), builds the fal model + input (reference-image/model-3d carry the reference as `image_url`), runs a real fal.ai **queue** request (submit → poll status → fetch result, with retry/backoff), and extracts the produced asset URL per model shape (`images[]`/`video`/`model_mesh`) + a metered € cost. - The HTTP transport is an injectable `FalTransport` so `generate` + the pure helpers (`composeFalInput`/`extractFalAsset`/`liveMediaCostCents`) are unit-tested with FIXTURES — no key, no network. The real transport (`realFalTransport`) is used by default. - `available()` still gates on `FAL_KEY`: no key → the registry never calls `generate` and returns the valid-shaped stub, so the dummy-data pipeline stays green.

chunks.title: 0080-real-voice-music-gen
chunks.text: ADR 0080: 0080-real-voice-music-gen. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #2: the ElevenLabs `generate()` returned `media.notImplemented` and music had no real provider. This item writes the REAL code (mirroring M1's fal pattern) behind `available()`. Decision: - **ElevenLabs (voice + sfx):** live `generate()` composes the input (text = style + prompt + extra; voice id from params/env), calls the ElevenLabs REST API (tts → `/text-to-speech/<voice>`, sfx → `/sound-generation`) which returns raw audio BYTES, and persists them via a new `server/media/store.ts` (`data/media/<uuid>.mp3` → a served `/media/...` url). Transport injectable → fixture-tested. - **Suno (music):** a NEW dedicated provider (`server/media/providers/suno.ts`) — `MediaProviderId` gains `'suno'`, registered in the registry, and `music` in the assignments now defaults to `'suno'`. Suno returns a HOSTED audio URL (submit → poll → url), so no local persistence. Transport injectable. - **Shared:** `composeMediaPrompt` moved to `server/media/prompt.ts` (fal re-exports it) so all three adapters compose style/extra identically.

chunks.title: 0081-real-llm-parsing
chunks.text: ADR 0081: 0081-real-llm-parsing. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #6: the "real" LLM lane was half-stub — `parseLiveScript` was a trivial one-beat-per-line split, and `analyzeReferenceVideo` ALWAYS used the canned stub blueprint even when the model responded. So adding a key wouldn't have produced structured beats. Decision: - New `server/content/jsonParse.ts`: `extractJson` robustly pulls the first JSON object out of an LLM response (```json fences, prose-wrapped, string-aware brace matching) — never throws (→ null on miss). `coerceBeats` maps a model's `beats` array into `{text, visualPrompt}[]`, tolerant of missing fields. - `parseLiveScript` (script.ts) now prefers the requested JSON (`{body, beats:[…]}`) and falls back to the line-based parse when the model returned prose. The prompt appends a `SCRIPT_FORMAT` directive. - `parseBlueprint` (referenceVideo.ts) parses a real `{pacing, styleHint, beats}` blueprint; the caller uses it when present and falls back to the stub only when there's no key OR nothing usable came back. The prompt appends a `BLUEPRINT_FORMAT` directive. - Both parsers are exported + pure → unit-tested.

chunks.title: 0082-real-ffmpeg-render
chunks.text: ADR 0082: 0082-real-ffmpeg-render. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #3: assembly was a DB row + a fake `stub://render/...` URL — no Remotion, no ffmpeg, no real file, and no way to download the result. Decision: - New `server/content/render.ts`: `buildFfmpegPlan` (pure) builds an ffmpeg **concat-demuxer** slideshow (one image per beat for its duration, last image repeated per the demuxer quirk) + an optional audio track (h264/yuv420p, scaled/padded to 1280×720, `-shortest`). `renderTimeline` localizes each asset (a `/media/<file>` used directly, an http(s) URL downloaded + persisted, a `stub://` URL not renderable), writes the concat list, and runs ffmpeg **in a Docker container** (`jrottenberg/ffmpeg`, MEDIA_DIR mounted at `/media`). The runner is injectable for tests. No hosted API → costCents 0. - **Degrade, don't fail:** when nothing is renderable (dummy `stub://` assets) or ffmpeg/Docker is unavailable, `renderTimeline` returns a typed `ok:false` and `assembleContent` falls back to the valid-shaped stub render asset — the dummy pipeline stays green without Docker/keys. - New `server/media/download.ts` — `GET /media/<uuid-file>` streams a produced media file (M2 audio + the render mp4) from the store; the unguessable uuid filename is the capability, with a hard path-traversal guard (`safeMediaPath`). Registered at boot (origin-exempt, like the build download).

chunks.title: 0083-real-publishing-oauth
chunks.text: ADR 0083: 0083-real-publishing-oauth. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #4: YouTube/TikTok "posts" were fake `stub://` urls — no OAuth, no upload. Decision: - New `server/content/publishOAuth.ts`: PURE request builders — `buildAuthUrl` (connect redirect), `buildExchangeRequest` (code→token), `buildUploadRequest` (YouTube resumable init / TikTok PULL_FROM_URL, bearer auth) — plus `parseTokenResponse` (flat + TikTok-nested). Transports wrap them with fetch (injectable; the live round-trip is the deferred post-keys e2e). - **Token storage** is ENCRYPTED via `secretBox` in the per-workspace `EnvVar` store (`__publish_<platform>`, `secret:true`) — no schema change, so no `db:push`/backend-kill. `connectPublishPlatform` exchanges the code + stores; `getConnection` decrypts. - `publishAsset` now runs a REAL upload with the decrypted token when the workspace is connected; a missing connection OR an upload failure degrades to the dummy post (never loses the consented intent). The B-23 gate is unchanged: `publishAsset` still only runs after a publish suggestion is accepted (Conductor).

chunks.title: 0084-content-ui-reach
chunks.text: ADR 0084: 0084-content-ui-reach. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #1: there was NO content UI — no `content` view, no nav item, no route; the `snapshot.content` loaded into the provider was read by NOTHING (dead state). The whole content lane was invisible + unusable in the app. Decision: - A `content` nav item (Studio group, `wand-magic-sparkles`) + a real `src/workspaces/content/page.tsx` route (the generic `pathForView`/`viewFromPath` already route `content` → `/workspaces/content`; `VIEW_LABELS` gains `content`). `WsView` already accepted `(string & {})`, so no type change. - The page renders a **content board**: 6 pipeline columns (idea → script → media → assemble → review → publish, mirroring server `CONTENT_STAGES`) reading `content.pieces` by `stageId`, each piece a card (title, format chip, status dot), plus a media **€-budget** summary bar (spent/cap/alert from `content.mediaBudget`). Clear empty-state for first-time users. All text via `useTranslator` (`workspaces.content.*`, 16 keys × en/nl/de/fr); only theme tokens + semantic status colors.

chunks.title: 0085-content-create-ui
chunks.text: ADR 0085: 0085-content-create-ui. U1 made the content lane reachable (board). U2 gives a piece a detail view with the generation controls a non-technical user needs — and wires the FIRST content control-op that fires from the UI. Decision: - **One generic sync route** `contentControl_server_v1.ts` dispatches the content-op family (whitelisted: create/advance/archive + every gen op + assemble + request-publish) through the shared `dispatchControlSync` (RBAC + single-writer Conductor, B-23). A type-guard narrows the op to `ControlOp` — no cast. (Content ops previously had backend cases + tests but no client route.) - **Client method** `runContentOp(op, contentProjectId, payload)` on the workspaces ctx fires `workspaces/contentControl` and refetches; typed on `WorkspacesCtx`. - **`content/[pieceId]/page.tsx`** — a piece detail: header (format/stage/status), a "creative direction" panel (style + free-form instructions + reference URL), and a grid of generation actions (script · voice · images · reference-image · short-form · music · sfx · 3D · assemble). Each action fires its control-op **behind a `menuHandler.confirm`** with a cost warning (budget-aware). All text i18n ×4 (`workspaces.content.*`, 41 keys); theme tokens only.

chunks.title: 0086-content-settings-setup
chunks.text: ADR 0086: 0086-content-settings-setup. `GAP_ANALYSIS.md` content #5: the media €-budget was computed but never shown, and there was no way to enter provider keys or a provider override from the app. Decision: - New `save-media-provider` control-op — stores an ENCRYPTED provider API key (`secretBox` → EnvVar `__provider_key_<providerId>`, `secret:true`) and/or a per-feature provider override (EnvVar `__media_provider_<feature>`). RBAC: `workspaceSettings`. (Per-workspace key CONSUMPTION by the adapters is a follow-up; this persists + lets the settings UI show what's configured.) - A `contentSettings_server_v1.ts` sync route dispatches the workspace-settings content ops (edit-media-budget / save-media-provider / save-style), whitelisted, via `dispatchControlSync` (B-23). Client methods `editMediaBudget` / `saveMediaProvider` on the ctx. - `content/settings/page.tsx` — a first-run **setup flow** (guided banner + a link to the KEY_SETUP_GUIDE + a money warning), a **provider-key form** (Fal / ElevenLabs / Suno / Gemini; password inputs, never shown back), and a media **€-budget form** (enable + cap in € + alert %, prefilled from `content.mediaBudget`). Reachable via a Settings button on the content board. i18n ×4; theme tokens only.

chunks.title: 0087-content-insights-brand
chunks.text: ADR 0087: 0087-content-insights-brand. The content-analytics fold (F5.1) + the style library + per-channel brand were computed/stored but never surfaced. U4 exposes them and lets a creator tune the brand. Decision: - **Snapshot extension:** `ContentSnapshot` gains `analytics` (from `computeContentAnalytics` over the workspace's pieces + media spend + publish jobs), `styles` (StylePreset — this workspace's + the global defaults), and `channels` (id/name/platform/brandVoice). Built in `workspaceSnapshot.ts`. - **`content-edit-brand` control-op** — updates a `Channel.brandVoice` + re-indexes the snippet into brand-RAG (`indexChannelBrand`, F5.1) so every generation for the channel can ground on it. RBAC: `workspaceSettings`; dispatched via the `contentSettings` route (B-23); ctx method `editChannelBrand`. - **`content/insights/page.tsx`** — an analytics dashboard (pieces/done/published/spend stat cards + pieces-by-stage bars + cost-by-feature), the style library (built-in vs custom), and a per-channel brand-voice editor. Reachable via an Insights button on the content board. i18n ×4; theme tokens only.

chunks.title: 0088-key-setup-guide
chunks.text: ADR 0088: 0088-key-setup-guide. The Depth Program wrote the real gen/render/publish code behind each `available()` gate. Turning it on needs real keys + budget — and that step must be safe + clear for a non-technical user, with the money risk spelled out. Decision: `docs/KEY_SETUP_GUIDE.md` — per provider (Fal, ElevenLabs, Suno, Gemini, YouTube, TikTok): where to get the key, where to put it (the encrypted in-app settings form OR `.env.local`), the env var names, and a **cost warning** (video/3D are the expensive ones; set a €-cap first). It leads with the two load-bearing rules: `WORKSPACES_ENC_KEY` is a boot requirement (H2), and set a media €-budget cap before adding any key. Linked from the U3 settings setup flow. ffmpeg render (Docker, no key) + the safe dummy-mode default are documented so the reader understands what already works without keys.

chunks.title: 0089-typecheck-gate-and-json-input
chunks.text: ADR 0089: 0089-typecheck-gate-and-json-input. `npm run build` is `vite build`, which transpiles per-file and does **not** type-check the project. The real full-program check is `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`), and it was **red**: 20 errors that had accumulated invisibly because CI/commits only ran vite + eslint. Most were typed data (a domain interface array, a `Record<string, unknown>`) being written into a Prisma `Json` column, which demands `Prisma.InputJsonValue` — a type an `interface`-shaped value can never satisfy (no index signature) even though the data is valid JSON at runtime. The rest were small nullability / union / prop-shape drifts (a nav item without its `group`, a `Dropdown` built with `label` instead of `item`, a fetch header union with optional-undefined members, a stage lookup that could be `undefined`). Decision: 1. **`npm run typecheck` (tsc) is a mandatory pre-delivery gate**, run per item alongside `lint` + `build` + `ai:lint`. Vite's per-file transpile is not a substitute for whole-program type safety. 2. **Typed data destined for a Prisma `Json` column goes through `server/util/json.ts` `jsonInput()`** — a deep-clone (`structuredClone`) that widens the value to `Prisma.InputJsonValue` **without a cast**. This honours the standing "no `as any` / `as unknown as T`" rule (Rule 21): the clone is a genuine structural coercion, and being a copy it is also safe to store. Every other error was fixed at its typing source (reorder so a `const` is narrowed

chunks.title: 0090-deterministic-test-provider-world
chunks.text: ADR 0090: 0090-deterministic-test-provider-world. The dev env now carries real media/AI provider keys (`.env.local`, resolved from the secret-manager), which the user added so the app can be exercised live. But the existing unit/integration suite was written for the **stub** world — deterministic, free, CI-safe (exact beat counts, `stub://…` urls, a `ai.providerUnavailable` path). With keys present, every provider's `available()` flipped to TRUE and those tests took the LIVE path (real HTTP → variable output / 401 on a pointer that isn't a real key). Simply unsetting the keys in the test harness didn't hold: importing any server module pulls in `@luckystack/core`, whose boot runs **dotenvx with `override:true`**, re-injecting the raw `.env.local` provider **pointers** over whatever the harness had cleared. Decision: The default test world is **stub**; a live-AI test **opts in**. - `tests/_helpers.mts` triggers the framework's dotenvx boot itself (`await import('@luckystack/core')`) and unsets the provider keys **after** it — dotenvx runs once (module then cached), so the clear sticks for every later server import. - `db()` additionally re-clears after `initSecretManager` (which resolves the pointers to the real keys and injects them), **stashing** the resolved values first. - `enableLiveProviders()` restores the stashed real keys for a live test and forces `WS_MEDIA_CHEAP=1` so a live run costs cents, not euros. It returns which providers actually have a key so a test can ski

chunks.title: 0091-per-workspace-media-keys
chunks.text: ADR 0091: 0091-per-workspace-media-keys. The in-app content Settings key-form (`save-media-provider`, ADR 0086) stores each provider key encrypted as `EnvVar __provider_key_<providerId>` and each per-feature provider choice as `EnvVar __media_provider_<feature>`. But `runMediaGeneration` read keys **only from `process.env`** — every provider's `available()` / transport read `process.env.FAL_KEY` etc. directly. So an env key worked, but a key entered in the app UI did nothing (it was stored, never consumed). FIX-A closes that. Decision: Keys are **threaded through the request**, not read from a global: - `MediaGenerationRequest` gains an optional `apiKey`; `MediaProvider.available(apiKey?)` takes an optional key. Each provider resolves `apiKey ?? process.env.<KEY>` — an explicit per-workspace key wins, env is the fallback. - Each provider's injectable transport gains a trailing `apiKey` param (the provider passes the already-resolved key). Test fixtures inject a transport with the *old* (fewer-param) signature, which stays assignable — so the fixture-based provider tests are unaffected. - `server/media/workspaceKeys.ts` `loadWorkspaceMediaConfig(prisma, workspaceId)` reads the two EnvVar families in one query and **decrypts** the keys via the shared `secretBox` (fail-closed: a bad blob → no key → stub). `runMediaGeneration` calls it whenever `req.workspaceId` is set, merges the stored per-feature override under any explicit `overrides` arg, resolves the provider, and passes th

chunks.title: 0092-publishing-oauth-connect-flow
chunks.text: ADR 0092: 0092-publishing-oauth-connect-flow. M5 (ADR 0083) built the *server* half of YouTube/TikTok publishing — `buildAuthUrl`, the code→token exchange, encrypted per-workspace token storage, `connectPublishPlatform`, and `publishAsset`. But it was **unreachable from the app**: there was no OAuth-callback HTTP route (so a user could never complete a connect) and no UI to request a publish (the `content-request-publish` op needs an `assetId` the UI never supplied). Publishing existed but nothing could invoke it (FIX-C). Decision: Two HTTP routes + two UI affordances close the loop: - **`GET /content/oauth/<platform>/start?ws=<id>`** — session-authed + `workspaceSettings`-gated; 302s to the platform consent screen with an encrypted `state`. - **`GET /content/oauth/<platform>/callback?code&state`** — origin-exempt (an external redirect has no Origin); decodes the state, exchanges the code, stores the token, 302s back to `/content/settings`. - The **`state`** is `encryptSecret({workspaceId,userId,platform,exp})` (secretBox/AES-GCM): CSRF-safe (unforgeable) and it carries the workspace across the external round-trip. `redirect_uri` comes from `WS_PUBLIC_URL` (or is derived from the forwarded host in dev) and must match the registered app. - **Settings** gains a Publishing-connections section (connect button / connected badge, from a new `snapshot.content.publishTargets`). **Piece-detail** shows a publish button per connected platform on a finished render, firing `content-reques

chunks.title: 0093-live-ai-verification
chunks.text: ADR 0093: 0093-live-ai-verification. The whole AI surface had only ever run against STUBS (deterministic, free). With the real provider keys now in the env (resolved via the secret-manager), the overnight goal was to prove EVERY AI-driven feature produces REAL output — and fix whatever the live run exposed. Running live is opt-in and costs money, so it must not be part of the default suite (ADR 0090). Decision: - **`tests/live/liveAi.live.mts`** (named `.live.mts`, NOT `.test.mts`, so `npm run test` never runs it) exercises every backend with `enableLiveProviders()` + `WS_MEDIA_CHEAP`, retrying each call (flaky-live policy) before it counts as a failure. Coverage: - **Gemini text (15/15 features):** the two gemini-native features (`script`, `reference-video-analysis`) plus every `claude-cli` feature FORCED to gemini via the provider override (ADR 0007) — a headless way to prove each feature's dispatch + real generation without the subscription-billing PTY (invariant #6; the PTY coding path is verified manually). - **Media:** fal (image / reference-image / video / avatar), elevenlabs (tts / sfx), suno (music). - **Live-surfaced provider bugs fixed** (the stub tests never hit the real API contracts): - **tts 404** — the default voice was the *name* `Rachel`; ElevenLabs needs the voice **id**. Default is now the real Rachel id (`21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM`). - **reference-image 422** — flux `image-to-image` rejects `image_size` (it derives size from the input) and requires `num_infere

chunks.title: 0094-premium-motion-layer
chunks.text: ADR 0094: 0094-premium-motion-layer. The overnight goal asked for a "premium feel" with clean animations everywhere, plus clarity + a consistent, trusted look for first-time users. The workspaces UI already had a mature shared primitives kit (`primitives.tsx`: WsButton/IconButton/Tabs/SectionCard/EmptyState/InfoDot/StatusPill/PopMenu…) and a shared motion module (`motion.tsx`: spring presets + Popover/Sheet/Backdrop, with global `MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"`). So consistency was largely a solved problem — the risk was *adding* animation, which if done per-page and blind (no browser to verify) tends to look busy or janky. Decision: Deliver the premium feel through the SHARED layer, in the fewest, safest places: - **One shell-level page transition.** `PageTransition` (in `motion.tsx`) wraps the routed content in `WorkspacesShell`, keyed on the route — every one of the ~19 pages gets the same snappy fade+lift on navigation from a SINGLE call site (`mode="wait"`, 0.17s, so pages never overlap). No per-page churn. - **Tactile primitives.** `WsButton`/`IconButton` gain a `motion-safe:active:scale` press — a universal micro-interaction that propagates to every screen through the shared components. - **A `Reveal` stagger primitive is provided but NOT force-applied.** Because the page already animates in via `PageTransition`, stacking a per-item reveal inside it would double-animate and read as busy. `Reveal` is available for a deliberate, browser-verified opt-in later. All moti

chunks.title: 0095-suno-api-integration
chunks.text: ADR 0095: 0095-suno-api-integration. ADR 0093 left an open question: live music generation 503'd because the Suno provider pointed at `https://api.suno.ai/v1` — not a real host. The user supplied the docs for the Suno API they actually have a key for: **`api.sunoapi.org`** (a Suno-proxy). The old provider also used the wrong flow (`/clips/<id>`) and field names. Decision: Rewrite `realMusicTransport` to the `api.sunoapi.org/api/v1` contract: - **Submit:** `POST /generate` with `{ prompt, customMode:false, instrumental:false, model, callBackUrl }` → `{ code:200, data:{ taskId } }`. `model` defaults to **`V5`** (fastest); the callback is required by the API but unused (we poll), so any URL satisfies it. - **Poll:** `GET /generate/record-info?taskId=…` → `data.status` (PENDING → TEXT_SUCCESS → SUCCESS) with the track under **`data.response.sunoData[0]`**. The full mp3 is `audioUrl` (at SUCCESS); `streamAudioUrl` appears earlier (TEXT_SUCCESS) as a playable fallback — we return whichever is present first, so a track is usable in ~20s instead of ~100s. - `SUNO_BASE` / `SUNO_MODEL` / `SUNO_CALLBACK_URL` are env-overridable (documented in `.env.local_template`). Live-verified: real `audioUrl` returned. The registry stub-fallback (no key) is unchanged, and the injectable-transport fixture tests are unaffected (the transport interface is the same).

chunks.title: 0096-fal-transport-robustness
chunks.text: ADR 0096: 0096-fal-transport-robustness. Trying to get `model-3d` (fal `triposr`) working live surfaced two real defects and one environmental truth: 1. **The fal queue fetches had no timeout.** A stalled connection hung a whole generation *forever* — a live model-3d probe ran >15 min with no progress and had to be killed. 2. **On poll-timeout the loop fell through** to fetch the response URL anyway, which returns the confusing "Request is still in progress" **400** instead of a clear timeout error. 3. **triposr's real blocker is fal-side QUEUE CONGESTION, not our poll budget.** A controlled diagnostic showed the job stuck at `queue_position: 8` and *not moving* over a minute — so bumping `FAL_POLL_MAX` (the user's hypothesis) does not help while the queue is backed up. Decision: - **`falFetch`** wraps every fal fetch (submit + status poll + result) in an `AbortController` with a hard `FAL_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 30s) — a hung connection now aborts instead of blocking indefinitely. - **Clean poll-timeout:** the poll loop tracks completion and throws `fal poll timeout` when the budget is exhausted, instead of fetching an incomplete result (the misleading 400). - **`FAL_POLL_MAX` default raised 60 → 120** (× 2s = 4 min) so a slow-but-*moving* queue still completes; `FAL_MODEL_3D` remains an env override for a faster/less-congested 3D model.

chunks.title: 0097-workspace-modules
chunks.text: ADR 0097: 0097-workspace-modules. A new workspace was always **name-only**, then dropped the user straight into a dev-centric shell: a full nav rail (Board, Backlog, Terminals, Pipeline, …), a seeded "Connect your GitLab project" ticket, and a Settings → Repository tab prompting for a repo link + a generated Dockerfile. But Workspaces is now an all-in-one AI content platform — many users want it **only** as a marketing/AI image+video tool, or **only** to design some UIs, and should never be asked to link a codebase or build a Dockerfile. The user also wanted the split to be a *starting preset*, not a rigid bundle: a Development workspace must be able to add just the Interviewer later. Decision: - A workspace stores `enabledSections: String[]` (`Workspace` model) — the resolved set of gateable nav-section ids. **Empty ⇒ legacy / all-on** (every pre-module workspace keeps every section). - Three shippable **modules** are pure presets (`src/workspaces/_data/modules.ts`): **Development** (board/backlog/terminals/activity/sources/pipeline/scheduled — the only lane needing a repo + Dockerfile), **Content & Marketing** (content/marketing), **Design** (designer/interviewer). At creation the user picks modules; the client resolves them to section ids and sends those. - Storage is **per-section**, not per-module, so individual sections toggle independently after creation (a Dev workspace can add the lone Interviewer). The settings "Modules" tab is a per-section toggle grid grouped by m

chunks.title: 0098-queue-aware-media-generation
chunks.text: ADR 0098: 0098-queue-aware-media-generation. fal media jobs (image/video/3d, notably triposr) can sit in the provider QUEUE before they start processing (ADR 0096 found triposr stuck at `queue_position: 8`). The old flow discarded fal's `IN_QUEUE`/`IN_PROGRESS` distinction + `queue_position` entirely, persisted the `MediaJob` already as `done`, and surfaced results only via the caller's post-completion `refetch()` — there was **no elapsed timer and no queue signal at all**. The user asked for queue support in the UI + timer logic so the timer waits for the queue instead of starting while the job is only queued. Decision: End-to-end queue awareness, respecting B-23 (the Conductor stays the single writer — media gen runs inline on its chain; we only add intermediate writes + socket emits within the same op): - **Provider reports progress.** `MediaGenerationRequest.onProgress?(p)` carries `{ state: 'queued'|'running', queuePosition? }`. `server/media/providers/fal.ts` reads `queue_position` + the `IN_QUEUE`→`IN_PROGRESS` transition in its poll loop and fires `queued` (on entry / position change) then `running` ONCE the job is picked up. - **Job lifecycle is persisted.** `MediaJob` gains `queuePosition Int?` + `startedAt DateTime?`. `server/content/mediaAsset.ts` creates the `ContentAsset` + `MediaJob` as **`queued` up front**, transitions `queued → running(@startedAt) → done` (progress writes serialized onto a chain awaited before the final write so they can't race completion),

chunks.title: 0099-queue-aware-all-flows-and-workspace-sync
chunks.text: ADR 0099: 0099-queue-aware-all-flows-and-workspace-sync. ADR 0098 made the *generic* media path (avatar/music/sfx/3d) queue-aware. But the specialised content flows (per-beat images, voice, short-form, reference-image, ffmpeg render) still used the old synchronous "create-as-done" path with no queued state and no broadcast, so other workspace members saw nothing live for them. Beyond that, the realtime layer had two robustness holes: (1) a client that briefly disconnects **misses every delta and is dropped from the room** with no recovery, and (2) the structural content mutations (piece create/advance/archive, script gen, settings) broadcast **nothing** — they reached only the caller's own refetch. The user asked for *all* flows queue-aware, everything synced to everyone across the workspace, and race conditions covered. Decision: - **One shared lifecycle helper** — `server/content/queuedMediaJob.ts:runQueuedMediaAsset`. It creates the `MediaJob` + `ContentAsset` as `queued` up front, threads a serialized queue→running `onProgress`, finalizes to `ready`/`error`, and broadcasts a content-asset delta at every transition. All five media flows (`mediaAsset`, `images` [per-beat loop], `voice`, `shortForm`, `referenceImage`) delegate to it, each supplying only its specifics via hooks (`onComplete` → `Beat.imageAssetId`; `finalizeMetadata` → voice timing map / short-form hook+captions). `assembly` (ffmpeg render, no provider queue) gets a `processing`→`ready` asset + broadcast manua

chunks.title: 0100-media-cost-transparency
chunks.text: ADR 0100: 0100-media-cost-transparency. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **Q1**. `estimateMediaCostCents` was computed server-side (used only by the budget guards) and never reached the UI: the generation confirm showed a number-free "may cost money" warning, and spend was visible only as a workspace total (retrospectively, on Insights). A user could not tell that a `video-gen` (40¢) costs 20× a `tts` (2¢) until after paying — a pay-first, blind experience. Decision: - The per-feature € estimate table (`STUB_COST_CENTS`, the single source of truth) is exposed via a new `mediaCostTable()` and carried in the content snapshot (`ContentSnapshot.mediaCosts`). The piece UI shows a "≈ €X" chip on each metered generation action and folds the estimate into the confirm body (per-item actions like per-beat images show "≈ €X / item"). Non-metered actions (script/assemble) show no chip. - Per-piece spend is surfaced (`ContentPieceSummary.spentCents`, grouped from the `MediaSpend` rows the system already records per `contentProjectId`) and shown on the piece header.

chunks.title: 0101-brand-product-grounding
chunks.text: ADR 0101: 0101-brand-product-grounding. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **Q2**. The channel brand voice a user typed was indexed into brand-RAG but `retrieveChannelBrand` was never consumed by any generation (dead), and there was no place to set a persistent "what we do / who our audience is / always mention X" so the AI stays on-brand. A user had to retype direction into the free-text extra-instructions box every single time. Decision: - A new `Workspace.productContext` field holds the persistent brand/product context, editable in the content settings (a new `content-edit-product` control-op, single-writer). - A single helper `buildBrandContext(prisma, workspaceId, contentProjectId?)` composes the workspace product context + the owning channel's `brandVoice` (read directly — deterministic, key-less, always available; not the embedding-dependent RAG path). - It is folded into **every creative generation at one choke-point each**: media via the shared `runQueuedMediaAsset` helper (grounds all image/video/3d/voice/music/sfx/reference flows) + `composeMediaPrompt` (prepended first); text via `generateScript`'s system prompt.

chunks.title: 0102-style-manager
chunks.text: ADR 0102: 0102-style-manager. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **Q3**. The `save-style` control-op + `StylePreset` model existed, but **no UI called it**: the piece page had a free-text style box where the user typed a key that had to exactly match a seeded preset (silently ignored otherwise). Users couldn't create, name, edit, or delete their own styles, and had to guess magic strings. Decision: - A **style manager** section in content settings: lists every style (global builtins read-only; per-workspace ones editable/deletable), with a create form (feature + key + label + system prompt). Backed by the existing `save-style` op + a new **`delete-style`** op (removes a per-workspace style; builtins are filtered out). - The snapshot's `ContentStyleSummary` now carries `systemPrompt` so the manager can show/edit it. - The piece page's free-text style box is replaced by a **Dropdown** of known style keys (deduped across features) + a "No style" option — pick by name, never guess.

chunks.title: 0103-workspace-ai-instruction
chunks.text: ADR 0103: 0103-workspace-ai-instruction. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **Q4**. There was no way to set a workspace-wide "how the AI should work here" — tone/rules/preferences that ALL AI features (dev + content) always follow. The dead `Workspace.handoffInstruction` field was named for a different (unbuilt) self-handoff purpose. Per-stage prompts steer one stage; the content brand context (Q2) steers creative facts — neither is a global behavioural steer. Decision: - A dedicated `Workspace.aiInstruction` field (not the mis-named `handoffInstruction` — a clean field avoids overloading a differently-purposed one; a conscious deviation from the program's literal "revive handoffInstruction" wording, Rule 3b). - It is prepended to **every** AI completion's system prompt at ONE choke-point — inside `runAiCompletion` (`server/ai/registry.ts`), which every feature already routes through — fetched best-effort via `getPrismaClient()` (the same singleton the media registry uses), so all 15 text features are steered without touching 13 call sites. - Editable in a new "AI" tab in workspace settings; persisted via a `save-ai-instruction` control-op (single-writer) broadcast back to the room.

chunks.title: 0104-gemini-workspace-key
chunks.text: ADR 0104: 0104-gemini-workspace-key. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **Q5**. The settings UI collected a Gemini key and stored it encrypted as `__provider_key_gemini`, but it was **consumed by nothing**: the media loader dropped it (gemini is not a `MediaProviderId`) and the text `gemini-api` provider read only `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY`. So a Gemini key entered in the UI did nothing, and Gemini was misleadingly listed among "media providers". The program also called for a per-feature media-provider picker — but there is exactly ONE provider per media feature today (fal / elevenlabs / suno), so a picker would be a useless single-option dropdown. Decision: - The `gemini-api` provider now **resolves its key per workspace**: `__provider_key_gemini` (decrypted) WINS over the env key, via `getPrismaClient()`. `AiProvider.available` gains an optional `workspaceId` (mirroring media's `available(apiKey?)`); `runAiCompletion` passes `req.workspaceId`. So a workspace key entered in the UI makes Gemini available + is used. - The settings keys are split into **Media providers** (fal/elevenlabs/suno) and an **AI text provider** (Gemini) so the user understands what each key drives. - The **per-feature media-provider picker is deferred** (logged): with one provider per feature it has nothing to choose. The `__media_provider_<feature>` override branch stays reachable for when alternate providers land.

chunks.title: 0105-stage-persona-in-ui
chunks.text: ADR 0105: 0105-stage-persona-in-ui. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **Q6**. A stage's `systemPrompt` (its agent persona → `--append-system-prompt`) and `definitionOfDone` existed in the model + snapshot, but the pipeline editor only exposed `customInstructions` + `promptTemplate` — so a user could tweak the task but not the agent's role/persona or its completion criterion (both stayed hardcoded from the default pipeline seed). The `save-stage-config` op even silently ignored `definitionOfDone`. Decision: - Add two fields to the pipeline stage editor's General tab: **AI persona (system prompt)** and **Definition of done**, editing `s.systemPrompt` / `s.definitionOfDone` (the `_sync` route already sends the whole cfg). - Fix the `save-stage-config` op to also persist `definitionOfDone` (it handled `systemPrompt` already).

chunks.title: 0106-media-upload-import
chunks.text: ADR 0106: 0106-media-upload-import. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **K1** — the enabler for bring-your-own-material + the editors. References were URL-only (paste a hosted url) and there was no way to bring your own image/video into a piece — every asset had to be AI-generated. The "Upload spec" button was a `noop`. No multipart parser is bundled. Decision: - A new authenticated HTTP route `POST /media/upload?ws=<id>&ext=<ext>` (`server/media/uploadRoute.ts`, registered in `server.ts` next to the download route). It reads the file as the **raw request body** (no multipart dep needed) into a bounded Buffer (64 MB cap), validates the extension against an image/video allowlist, and `persistMediaBytes(...)` → returns `{ url: '/media/<uuid>.<ext>', kind }`. Authed via the session token + membership-gated (`workTickets`) + tenant-scoped by the `ws` param. - A reusable `MediaUploadButton` + `uploadMedia()` client helper. The piece page uses it to (a) upload a reference for reference-conditioned gen (replacing URL-only), and (b) **import your own** image/video via a new `content-import-asset` control-op that creates a `ready` ContentAsset (no MediaJob) on the single-writer chain (B-23) and broadcasts the live delta.

chunks.title: 0107-doc-upload-infosource
chunks.text: ADR 0107: 0107-doc-upload-infosource. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **K2**. The Sources page "Upload spec" button was a `noop` — a user could not bring their own knowledge/house-rules docs for the AI to use; InfoSources only came from a linked git repo (`scan-docs`). Decision: - A new `create-info-source` control-op registers an uploaded doc as a `source: 'uploaded'` context-doc InfoSource (upsert by name, `enabled: false` by default — the user toggles it on). It returns the full context-doc list as the delta (same shape + client callback as `scan-docs`), via a new `addInfoDoc` `_sync` route + provider method. - The client reads the file's text (`File.text()`) and sends it — **no binary upload needed for text docs** (md/txt); the K1 `/media/upload` route is for binary media, this is plain text over the control channel.

chunks.title: 0108-creative-knowledge-grounding
chunks.text: ADR 0108: 0108-creative-knowledge-grounding. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **K3**. RAG retrieval was walled off from the creative features — only the dev stage-agent + reviewers called `retrieve()`; `script`/designer/marketer had no access to the user's uploaded docs (K2) or repo docs. So a user could upload house-style/product docs and the content AI still ignored them. Decision: - A `buildKnowledgeContext(prisma, workspaceId)` helper folds the workspace's **enabled** context-doc InfoSources (bounded: 2000 chars/doc, 6000 total) into a labelled grounding block, and `generateScript` prepends it (alongside the Q2 brand context). Deterministic + **key-less** — no embeddings needed; the user's enabled docs steer the script.

chunks.title: 0109-output-language
chunks.text: ADR 0109: 0109-output-language. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **K4**. Generated content was English-by-default — no way to choose the AI OUTPUT language (script/voice/copy in NL/DE/FR/…); the model just inferred it from the brief. (The app UI i18n is separate — this is the generated content's language.) Decision: - A `Workspace.outputLanguage` field (a language name, e.g. `Dutch`; empty = the model's default). It is prepended as a strong directive ("Write all output in Dutch.") to **every** AI completion's system prompt at the same single choke-point as the Q4 instruction (`workspaceAiPrefix` in `server/ai/registry.ts`). - Edited via a language Dropdown in the AI settings tab, persisted through the extended `save-ai-instruction` op (which now carries `aiInstruction` + `outputLanguage`). Voice/TTS follows because it reads the (now target-language) script.

chunks.title: 0110-text-provider-per-feature
chunks.text: ADR 0110: 0110-text-provider-per-feature. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **P1**. `resolveAssignment(feature, overrides)` was built to accept a per-workspace override map, but the `overrides` arg was **never fed** at any of the 13 `runAiCompletion` call sites — the seam was inert, and there was no UI. So every feature was locked to its hardcoded default provider. Decision: - A per-workspace override is stored as an EnvVar `__ai_provider_<feature>` (mirrors the media `__media_provider_<feature>` store), loaded by `loadWorkspaceAiOverrides` and **merged inside `runAiCompletion`** UNDER any explicit call-site override: `resolveAssignment(feature, { ...wsOverrides, ...overrides })`. This feeds the seam at ONE point — no call-site changes. - A `save-ai-provider` control-op + a `_sync` route (returns the full override map → `snap.aiOverrides`), and a per-feature provider Dropdown in the AI settings tab for the curated non-coding features (Default / Claude / Gemini).

chunks.title: 0111-gemini-model-temperature
chunks.text: ADR 0111: 0111-gemini-model-temperature. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **P2**. There was no generation-param tuning anywhere: Gemini read only the process-wide `GEMINI_MODEL` env and sent no temperature; Claude-CLI has no model/temperature concept at all (it drives the interactive subscription-billed PTY — model is subscription-determined, PTY-billing invariant). Decision: - Per-workspace `Workspace.geminiModel` + `Workspace.geminiTemperature` (strings; empty = env/model default). The `gemini-api` provider resolves them per workspace in one config read (`resolveGeminiConfig`, folded with the Q5 key read) and sends `generationConfig.temperature` (clamped 0–2) + the chosen model. - Edited in the AI settings tab (model input + temperature input), persisted through the extended `save-ai-instruction` op (now carries instruction + language + geminiModel + geminiTemperature).

chunks.title: 0112-media-model-choice
chunks.text: ADR 0112: 0112-media-model-choice. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **P3**. The fal model per feature was **env-only** (`FAL_MODEL_*`, process-global); `falModelFor` ignored `req.params` for model selection, so a user couldn't choose a faster/low-poly/cheaper model per generation or per workspace. Decision: - `composeFalInput` now consults **`req.params.model`** (a per-request model id) → picks the fal model, and strips `model` from the input body (it's a routing param, not a fal input field). Falls back to the env/default. - A **per-workspace** model override is stored as `__media_model_<feature>` (mirrors the provider-override store); `loadWorkspaceMediaConfig` loads it (`cfg.models`), and `runMediaGeneration` injects it into `params.model` (the caller's own `params.model` still wins). Saved via the extended `save-media-provider` op ('default' clears it). - The content settings expose an advanced **free-text model id per feature** (empty = the built-in default, shown as the placeholder), surfaced from the snapshot (`content.mediaModels`).

chunks.title: 0113-content-regenerate-variations
chunks.text: ADR 0113: 0113-content-regenerate-variations. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **I1**. Content assets were pure one-shot: no regenerate, no variations, no "make it more X" — if you didn't like a result your only recourse was to fire a whole new generation from the direction inputs. The MediaJob stored the input, but nothing re-used it. Decision: - A `content-regenerate` control-op: given an asset id, it loads the asset's `MediaJob` (feature + prompt + referenceUrl + style), and re-runs `generateMediaAsset` **N times** (`count`, 1–4) with an optional `tweak` appended to the instructions — each variation goes through the queue-aware lifecycle (queued → processing → ready + live delta), so the timer/queue UX is identical to a fresh gen. - The asset card shows **Regenerate** + a variations (×3) button for a **`regenerable`** asset (a ready, AI-generated, non-imported asset — a new summary flag from `toContentAssetSummary`), using the piece's current free-form direction as the tweak. Behind the cost confirm (B-23; it spends).

chunks.title: 0114-content-version-lineage
chunks.text: ADR 0114: 0114-content-version-lineage. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **I2**. I1 added regenerate/variations, but the new assets were unlinked from the source — no way to tell which asset a variation came from, and no version grouping. Decision: - `ContentAsset.parentId` records the asset a variation was regenerated FROM. `content-regenerate` sets it on each new asset to the **root** of the lineage (if the source is itself a variation, chain to its parent so all variations share one root — a flat, not deep, tree). - The asset summary carries a `variant` flag (has a parent) → the card shows a small **Variant** badge, so the user sees originals vs regenerations at a glance.

chunks.title: 0115-studio-refine
chunks.text: ADR 0115: 0115-studio-refine. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **I4**. Studio's regenerate re-ran the same brief with no delta — a blind re-roll. The only way to steer a studio output was to edit the whole brief and regenerate; you couldn't say "make the landing page bolder". Decision: - `generateArtifact` takes an optional `tweak`; a pure `applyRefine(prompt, tweak)` appends it to the built prompt ("Refine with this specific direction: …") after the brand-seeded brief. Threaded through the `workspaces/studioGenerate` API + the client `generateArtifact(briefId, kind, tweak?)`. - The studio page has a single **Refine** input applied to every (re)generation — type "make it more playful", hit a generate/regenerate, and the direction is honoured.

chunks.title: 0116-web-push-pwa
chunks.text: ADR 0116: 0116-web-push-pwa. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **A1**, and the explicit `/goal` ask ("voeg ook de sw.js toe"). The product is phone-first (the human is a man-in-the-middle who approves + answers from their phone), but there was NO push at all: the `PushSubscription` model existed but nothing wrote or read it, there was no service worker, no manifest, no VAPID, and the settings toggle was cosmetic (a local `useState` with a "Fase 2" comment). Decision: - **Self-hosted env-VAPID** (decided OV-5). Keys live in `.env.local` (`WS_VAPID_PUBLIC/PRIVATE/SUBJECT`), documented in `.env.local_template`. `web-push` installed; imported **lazily** in `server/hooks/webPush.ts` (its API lands on `.default` under the ESM loader) so the server boots without it and a send failure never breaks the notification write it rides on. - **A dependency-free `public/sw.js`** (push → `showNotification`; `notificationclick` → focus/open) + `public/manifest.webmanifest`, both served at root by Vite's default `publicDir`. Registered from `main.tsx` on load; manifest linked from `index.html`. - **Two `_api` routes**: `pushConfig` delivers the PUBLIC VAPID key to the browser (the key can't reach the client via `config.ts` — its env reader is browser-safe-`undefined`, and no `VITE_` bridge is wired); `savePushSubscription` upserts the browser subscription keyed on the **authenticated** user + the (now `@unique`) endpoint. The settings toggle drives a real subscribe/unsubscribe (`pushSubscribe.ts`). - **Push

chunks.title: 0117-push-fanout-notifications
chunks.text: ADR 0117: 0117-push-fanout-notifications. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **A2**. A1 wired `sendWebPush` into the single assignment-notify choke-point only. The two other runtime notification sites — the automation `notify` action and `invoke-agent-role` (both a `createMany` fan-out over all members) — created in-app notifications but no push, so a member with the app closed missed automation + AI-suggestion events on their phone. Decision: - A `sendWebPushMany(prisma, userIds, payload)` helper (best-effort per user, never throws) added to `webPush.ts`. Wired in right after both `notification.createMany` sites in `executor.ts` so every in-app notification is mirrored to the members' devices. Same tag scheme (`ticket-<key>`) as A1 for coalescing.

chunks.title: 0118-push-per-type-preferences
chunks.text: ADR 0118: 0118-push-per-type-preferences. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **A3**. After A1/A2 every notification pushed to every subscribed device — all-or-nothing (the only control was subscribing or not). A user who wants assignment pushes but not automation noise had no way to tune it. Decision: - Three `User.preferences` booleans — `pushOnAssignment`, `pushOnAutomation`, `pushOnAiSuggestion` — all **opt-out** (default ON, matching the existing `notifyOnAssignment` bell convention). Added to the `updatePreferences` allow-list. - `sendWebPush` / `sendWebPushMany` take an optional `PushCategory`; a pure `pushCategoryAllowed(prefs, category)` gate suppresses a push only when that category is explicitly `false`. The three call sites pass their category (`assignment` / `automation` / `aiSuggestion`). - The settings notifications card shows the three per-type toggles, revealed once push is enabled.

chunks.title: 0119-autonomy-dials
chunks.text: ADR 0119: 0119-autonomy-dials. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **A4**. `PipelineStage.gateForApproval` gated a stage per-flag, but there was no UI and no coarse "ask me less / ask me more" control — a workspace couldn't say "just run everything" or "check with me at every step". The man-in-the-middle had a fixed cadence. Decision: - `Workspace.autonomyLevel` (default `gate-key-stages`) with three levels. A pure `resolveStageGate(stageGate, level)` in `stageRunner` computes the effective gate: `full-auto` → never gate (skip non-destructive approvals), `gate-every` → gate every stage, `gate-key-stages` → honour the stage's own `gateForApproval` (the prior behaviour). Used at BOTH gate decisions in the done-branch (advance + push-for-approval), so full-auto advances AND doesn't open an approval MR. - A `save-autonomy` control-op + `_sync` route + snapshot field + an AI-tab dropdown, mirroring the `save-sections` module-gating pattern.

chunks.title: 0120-needs-input-reping
chunks.text: ADR 0120: 0120-needs-input-reping. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **A5**. A real open question (`Ticket.needsInput`) parked FOREVER: the ticket waited, whoever opened it first answered, and nobody was actively told it was still waiting. For a phone-first man-in-the-middle that means a question can silently rot. Decision: - The watchdog sweep gains a third responsibility: for every ticket with a REAL `needsInput` banner, it baselines `Ticket.remindedAt` on first sight (no immediate ping), then **re-pings the assignee** (routing — `assigneeId`, falling back to `creatorId`) at most once per `WS_NEEDS_INPUT_REMIND_MIN` (default 120 min) via a `reminder` notification + a web-push. `remindedAt` is cleared on the answer path, so a fresh question starts a fresh clock. A pure `shouldRemind(remindedAt, now, intervalMs)` drives the timing (unit-tested; `now` injected).

chunks.title: 0121-export-formats-captions
chunks.text: ADR 0121: 0121-export-formats-captions. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **O1**. The video render was locked to a fixed 1280×720 / 30fps landscape plan — no vertical (9:16) format for TikTok/Shorts/Reels, no square, and the `captions` metadata that already exists was never exported as subtitle files. Decision: - `buildFfmpegPlan` takes an optional `RenderFormat`; `resolveRenderFormat(key)` maps `16:9` (1280×720, the default), `9:16` (720×1280 vertical), `1:1` (1080×1080) — the scale/pad target + fps come from the preset. `renderTimeline` accepts a `format` string and passes it through. Unknown/absent → the 16:9 default. - Pure `buildSrt(captions, totalMs)` + `buildVtt(captions, totalMs)` emit well-formed subtitle files by distributing the (untimed) caption LINES evenly across the duration.

chunks.title: 0122-post-scheduling
chunks.text: ADR 0122: 0122-post-scheduling. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **O3**. Publishing was immediate-only: accepting a publish suggestion posted right then. No way to queue a post for a future time (a content calendar). Decision: - `PublishJob.scheduledAt` + a `scheduled` status. The upload implementation was extracted into a `performUpload` helper (no job write) shared by both paths. `publishAsset` with a future `scheduledAt` parks a `scheduled` job (no post); an immediate publish posts + records a `done` job as before. - `runScheduledPublish(prisma, now)` fires every due (`scheduledAt <= now`) scheduled job through `performUpload` + flips it to `done`/`error`. `now` is injected for deterministic tests; a `startScheduledPublisher` interval runs it **leader-gated** (ADR 0015 — exactly one instance fires each due post), mirroring the watchdog loop. - Reschedule = updating `PublishJob.scheduledAt` (the loop honours the new time).

chunks.title: 0123-branding-watermark
chunks.text: ADR 0123: 0123-branding-watermark. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **O4** (branding). The render produced un-branded video — no way to stamp a logo watermark from the brand kit onto the output. Decision: - `buildFfmpegPlan` takes an optional `Watermark { file, position }`. When present it switches from the simple `-vf` scale path to a `-filter_complex` graph — `[0:v]<scale>[bg];[bg][N:v]overlay=<xy>[outv]` with explicit `-map [outv]` (+ `-map 1:a` when there's audio) — placing the logo in a corner (default bottom-right, 24px margin). `renderTimeline` localizes an optional `watermarkUrl` (a brand-kit logo) and skips it cleanly if it can't be localized. All pure + unit-tested.

chunks.title: 0124-per-platform-publish-variants
chunks.text: ADR 0124: 0124-per-platform-publish-variants. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **O2**. Publishing posted the piece TITLE to every platform with a hardcoded `private` visibility — no per-platform caption, hashtags, or privacy. Each network wants its own copy + settings. Decision: - A normalized `PublishVariant { caption?, hashtags?, privacy? }` with `privacy: 'public'|'unlisted'|'private'`. `buildUploadRequest` takes an optional `variant` and maps it to each platform's own vocabulary — YouTube `privacyStatus` (public/unlisted/private), TikTok `privacy_level` (PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE / SELF_ONLY; no "unlisted" → SELF_ONLY). A pure `composeCaption(title, variant)` builds the caption (override or title) + `#`-prefixed hashtags. - Variants are stored per-piece on `ContentProject.publishVariants` (a `{ [platform]: variant }` JSON). A pure `extractPublishVariant(json, platform)` validates + pulls the entry; `performUpload` threads it into the upload. Defaults preserve the prior behaviour (title-only, private).

chunks.title: 0125-outbound-webhook-action
chunks.text: ADR 0125: 0125-outbound-webhook-action. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **X2**. The automation `ActionExecutor` could only notify / emit-signal / start-stage / invoke-agent-role — all internal. There was no way for a workspace event to reach the user's OWN systems (post to their URL). Extensibility "plug the AI into the user's world" needs an egress. Decision: - A `webhook` `TriggerActionKind`: `executeTriggerAction` POSTs a compact event envelope (`{ event, ticketKey, payload, workspaceId }`) to a user-configured `params.url`. Requires `http(s)`; a non-2xx or a thrown request is an `error` outcome (best-effort — a bad webhook never wedges the pipeline, consistent with every other action). The poster is module-injectable (`__setWebhookPoster`) so it's tested offline. Surfaced in the AutomationPanel with a URL field.

chunks.title: 0126-custom-gemini-endpoint
chunks.text: ADR 0126: 0126-custom-gemini-endpoint. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **X4**. The Gemini endpoint was hardcoded to Google's `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta`. No way to point at a self-hosted / proxied / regional Gemini-compatible endpoint. (The coding agent stays `claude` in a PTY — the PTY-billing invariant — so this is non-coding-provider only.) Decision: - A per-workspace `Workspace.geminiBaseUrl` + a `WS_GEMINI_BASE_URL` env, resolved in `resolveGeminiConfig` (workspace override > env > Google default) alongside the P2 model/temperature read (one query). A pure `geminiEndpoint(baseUrl, model)` builds the `…/models/<model>:generateContent` URL, trimming trailing slashes. Edited in the AI-tab (a base-URL field) through the same `save-ai-instruction` op as the other Gemini settings.

chunks.title: 0127-mcp-integration-wiring
chunks.text: ADR 0127: 0127-mcp-integration-wiring. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **X1**. `renderStage` built the container `.mcp.json` from skill keys ONLY — a workspace's own `IntegrationTool.mcp.command` was stored but inert (never mounted), so an enabled integration did nothing for the agent. Decision: - `renderStage` now also emits one stdio MCP server per **enabled** integration tool: a pure `parseMcpCommand(cmd)` splits the command string into `{ command, args }`, `mcpKey(name)` sanitizes the server key, and the tool's credentials are injected as `env`. `stageRunner.loadMcpIntegrations` resolves each `IntegrationField.envVarId` to its EnvVar (decrypted) and passes the tools into the (still-pure) renderer. Skills + integrations coexist in one `.mcp.json`.

chunks.title: 0128-brand-kit-portability
chunks.text: ADR 0128: 0128-brand-kit-portability. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **R3**. Customization must not be trapped in one workspace: a workspace's brand library (palette / typography / voice / taglines / logo ideas) was `workspaceId`-locked with no way to move it to another workspace or share it. Decision: - A pure `parseBrandKit(raw)` validates/normalizes a portable JSON blob into the existing `BrandLibraryInput` (reusing the same `str`/`strArr`/palette validators as the artifact-promote path). `exportBrandKit(ws)` reads the library → a portable kit (no ids/timestamps/workspaceId); `importBrandKit(ws, raw)` upserts it via the existing `saveBrandLibrary`. Two membership-gated `_api` routes (`brandExport`/`brandImport`) carry the JSON string.

chunks.title: 0129-cheap-preview
chunks.text: ADR 0129: 0129-cheap-preview. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **S1**. `WS_MEDIA_CHEAP` (the fast/low-res/single-output mode) was an OPERATOR env only — all-or-nothing for the whole deployment. A user couldn't rehearse a single generation cheaply before spending on the full-quality run. Decision: - `cheapMode(reqCheap?)` is now on when the operator env is set OR a per-request flag asks for it. A `params.cheap === true` flag (a routing param, stripped from the fal input body like `params.model`) drives `falModelFor` (→ the fast `schnell` image model) + `cheapParams` (low steps / low resolution / single output) for that ONE request. The full-quality run is unaffected when the flag is absent.

chunks.title: 0130-undo-unpublish
chunks.text: ADR 0130: 0130-undo-unpublish. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **S2**. Archiving a piece and publishing a post were one-way: no restore, no retract. A safety net for reversible actions was missing. Decision: - `content-unarchive` sets `archived: false` (a soft-undo — the row was never deleted; archive is a flag). - `content-unpublish` flips the matching **done** `PublishJob` (by `assetId` + `platform`) to `unpublished` + broadcasts content-dirty. Both are `workTickets`-capability control-ops on the single-writer chain.

chunks.title: 0131-custom-ai-tasks
chunks.text: ADR 0131: 0131-custom-ai-tasks. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **E5**. The AI features were a closed set — a user could not author their own re-runnable AI task. The hard constraint: any such escape hatch must NOT introduce a new write verb or a direct writer (single-writer + the frozen structured-channel surface). Decision: - A `CustomAiTask` model (name + `promptTemplate` with `{{variables}}` + a read-only `lastOutput`). A new generic `custom-generate` `AiFeature` (Claude default, provider-per-feature-overridable via P1). A pure `renderTaskPrompt(template, vars)` substitutes the variables; `runCustomTask` renders + runs it through `runAiCompletion` and stores `lastOutput` ONLY. - Three control-ops on the single-writer chain: `save-custom-task` / `delete-custom-task` / `run-custom-task` (workTickets capability). Running is **propose/generate** — it produces output the user reads; it never writes authoritative state (verified: a run creates no tickets/assets). Surfaced as a "My AI tasks" panel (create / run / delete + output) fed from a new `snapshot.customTasks` field.

chunks.title: 0132-inpaint-feature
chunks.text: ADR 0132: 0132-inpaint-feature. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **E1** — the headline "circle a spot → change the colour / make it bigger" region editor. Its backend needs a media feature that takes a source image + a mask + an instruction and produces a region-edited image. No such feature existed (media was gen-only, no masking). Decision: - A new `inpaint` `MediaFeature` + a `maskUrl` on `MediaGenerationRequest`. `composeFalInput` builds the fal flux-inpaint input shape: `image_url` (the source, from `referenceUrl`) + `mask_url` (the mask, white = edit region) + the instruction as the `prompt`, routed to an **env-overridable** model (`FAL_MODEL_INPAINT`, default `fal-ai/flux-general/inpainting`). All the `Record<MediaFeature, …>` maps (kind / provider / cost / support) gained an `inpaint` entry (image kind, fal provider, ~5¢).

chunks.title: 0133-output-templates
chunks.text: ADR 0133: 0133-output-templates. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **O5**. The render format (aspect, watermark) had to be picked per generation (O1/O4). A user producing a repeatable format (e.g. "vertical Reels with a bottom-right logo") had no way to save + reuse that spec across pieces. Decision: - An `OutputTemplate` model (name + `format` [16:9/9:16/1:1] + `watermarkPosition`). `save-output-template` / `delete-output-template` control-ops (workTickets) validate the format/position + persist; the templates are exposed on `snapshot.outputTemplates` with client save/delete methods. A saved spec's `format` feeds the O1 `resolveRenderFormat` → `buildFfmpegPlan` render plan directly.

chunks.title: 0134-style-set-portability
chunks.text: ADR 0134: 0134-style-set-portability. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **R1** (save-as-template + apply). A workspace's user-authored `StylePreset` set was `workspaceId`-locked — no way to reuse a curated style library in another workspace. (The brand half of this reuse story shipped as R3/ADR 0128.) Decision: - A pure `parseStyleSet(raw)` validates a portable style JSON array (drops malformed entries; a missing label defaults to the key). `exportStyleSet(ws)` returns the workspace's **non-builtin** styles (no ids/timestamps/workspaceId); `importStyleSet(ws, raw)` upserts them by `feature`+`key` — never touching the builtin global defaults. Two membership-gated `_api` routes (`styleExport`/`styleImport`) carry the JSON.

chunks.title: 0135-cross-workspace-copy
chunks.text: ADR 0135: 0135-cross-workspace-copy. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **R2**. Customization was `workspaceId`-locked: even with the R1/R3 export/import, moving a style library + brand kit between two of the user's OWN workspaces meant a manual export-download-import round trip. A direct "copy to another workspace" was missing. Decision: - A `copy-workspace-assets` control-op (workspaceSettings) that copies the user-authored styles + the brand kit FROM a source workspace INTO the active one, **reusing** `exportStyleSet`/`importStyleSet` (R1) + `exportBrandKit`/`importBrandKit` (R3). The Conductor authorizes the **source** side too — the acting user must be a member of the workspace they copy FROM (not just the target the RBAC already gates).

chunks.title: 0136-public-api-pats
chunks.text: ADR 0136: 0136-public-api-pats. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **X3**. There was no way to drive a workspace from OUTSIDE the app — no token-gated API. The hard constraint: an external caller must respect the SAME single-writer + RBAC invariants as the in-app path (never a direct writer), and tokens must be scoped + revocable + never stored in the clear. Decision: - A `PersonalAccessToken` model storing only the **SHA-256 hash** (raw shown once at issue) + a display prefix + `scopes` + a `revoked` flag. `generateToken`/`hashToken`/`resolvePat` are the token layer; `driveViaPat(token, op, payload)` authenticates → checks the op's required scope → enqueues on the **single-writer Conductor** (same RBAC as the app — the PAT only authenticates + scopes, never writes directly). Only an allow-listed set of ops is exposed (`quick-add` = tickets:write, `content-create` = content:write). - Transport: a `POST /api/public/v1/op` custom route (origin-exempt, `Authorization: Bearer wsk_…` + a JSON `{ op, payload }`), + `issuePat`/`revokePat` membership-gated `_api` routes.

chunks.title: 0137-content-inpaint-op
chunks.text: ADR 0137: 0137-content-inpaint-op. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **E1**. ADR 0132 added the `inpaint` MediaFeature + `composeFalInput` mask plumbing. The remaining backend gap: a content-flow op that takes a source image + a mask + an instruction and produces a new region-edited asset (so the eventual canvas editor has a write path to call). Decision: - `generateMediaAsset` threads a `maskUrl` into the media request. A `content-inpaint` control-op (`{ contentProjectId, referenceUrl, maskUrl, prompt, parentAssetId? }`) runs the inpaint feature → a NEW asset, chained to the source via `parentId` (I2 lineage). No-ops without a mask/prompt. workTickets capability, single-writer.

chunks.title: 0138-image-region-editor
chunks.text: ADR 0138: 0138-image-region-editor. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **E1** — the headline "circle a spot → change the colour / make it bigger" editor. The backend (inpaint feature ADR 0132 + the content-inpaint op ADR 0137) was complete + tested; the missing piece was the canvas UI that lets a user DRAW the region → produce the mask the op consumes. Decision: - An `ImageRegionEditor` React component (OV-1 = Fabric.js): the source asset is the display background; a white free-draw brush paints the edit region. On apply, the strokes are exported as a **white-on-black mask** from a fresh `StaticCanvas` that only ever holds the cloned stroke paths — the source image never touches that canvas, so the export is never tainted (no CORS export failure). The mask PNG is uploaded via the K1 `/media/upload` route → a `maskUrl`, then `content-inpaint` (ADR 0137) region-edits into a new asset (I2 lineage). - Fabric is **lazily imported** (`await import('fabric')`) so it lands in its own chunk, never in a non-editor route bundle (OV-1). Surfaced as an "Edit region" button on ready image assets in the piece page.

chunks.title: 0139-image-editor-essentials
chunks.text: ADR 0139: 0139-image-editor-essentials. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **E2** — the essentials around the E1 region editor: adjustments + crop, non-destructive. Decision: - An `ImageEditor` component on the same Fabric.js canvas: brightness / contrast / saturation sliders applied as fabric image filters, exported as a NEW image asset (non-destructive — the original is untouched; the edit is imported via the tested `content-import-asset` op, appearing as a normal asset). It's a client-side transform (no provider, no spend). Fabric + its filters are lazily imported. An "Adjust" button on ready image assets, alongside E1's "Edit region".

chunks.title: 0140-video-timeline-reorder
chunks.text: ADR 0140: 0140-video-timeline-reorder. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **E3** — a video timeline: see the scenes (beats), reorder them, trim each. The render reads beats `orderBy: order` with a per-beat `durationMs`, but nothing let a user change the order or the on-screen time. Decision: - A `content-reorder-beats` control-op: given `[{ beatId, order?, durationMs? }]` it updates each beat's `order` (resequence) + `durationMs` (trim, clamped 0.5–30s). Because the assembly renders beats in `order` with each beat shown for its `durationMs`, this directly drives the ffmpeg plan (sequence + clip times) — verified by reordering + trimming and asserting the resulting `buildFfmpegPlan` concat list.

chunks.title: 0141-audio-mix-plan
chunks.text: ADR 0141: 0141-audio-mix-plan. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **E4** — an audio editor: trim + mix voice + music + sfx (music ducked under voice) into a single track the render consumes. The render had a single voice track only; no multi-track mix. Decision: - A pure `buildAudioMixPlan(tracks)` builds the ffmpeg `-filter_complex` that mixes N tracks — each with a per-track linear volume (voice ~1, music ducked ~0.25, sfx ~0.6) + an optional `atrim` — into one `[aout]` stream via `amix=inputs=N:duration=longest`. Returns the filter + the output map for the render to wire in.

chunks.title: 0142-setup-wizard
chunks.text: ADR 0142: 0142-setup-wizard. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **S3**. Configuration was forms-only — a new user had to find the media-key + budget settings across tabs to reach a working state. Decision: - A `SetupWizard` stepper (welcome → connect a media key → set a spend budget): each step fires the SAME single-writer control-op as the settings UI (`saveMediaProvider({ apiKey })` / `editMediaBudget`). The wizard is a friendlier front door, never a new writer. Opened from a "Quick setup" button on the workspace settings header.

chunks.title: 0143-premium-ux-sweep
chunks.text: ADR 0143: 0143-premium-ux-sweep. FREEDOM_PROGRAM item **S4** — a premium-UX sweep across every Fase Q–E screen (motion, empty-states/tooltips, phone-first, a11y, consistency via shared primitives + theme tokens, reduced-motion). Most of this was applied inline as each surface was built (theme tokens only, i18n on every string, `motion-safe:` tactile presses, shared `WsButton`/`Dropdown`/`Toggle` primitives). The gap: the new full-screen overlays (the editors, the wizard) were mouse-dismiss only. Decision: - A shared `useEscapeKey(onClose)` hook wired into the three new overlays (ImageRegionEditor, ImageEditor, SetupWizard) so they're keyboard-dismissible (a11y, §0b). The cross-cutting invariants — no untranslated JSX, no arbitrary colors — are enforced by `ai:lint`, which is **green repo-wide** across every new surface (the gate-able core of the §0b checklist).

chunks.title: 0144-honesty-fixes
chunks.text: ADR 0144: 0144-honesty-fixes. A 5-agent audit found the product's biggest "looks-done-but-isn't" risk: several paths returned a fake success. A publish with no connection (or a failed upload) was recorded `PublishJob.status:'done'` with a `stub://` url; a render that couldn't run (no keys/Docker) was recorded `ContentAsset.status:'ready', downloadable:true` with a `stub://render/...` url — a fake finished video; `claudeCli.available()` returned true whenever the bin was the bare name `'claude'`, even with the CLI not installed. And the whole suite runs against stubs with keys actively unset, so nothing proved a real artifact. Decision: - **Publish honesty:** `performUpload` returns a discriminated `real | stub | error`. A not-connected publish → `PublishJob.status:'stub'` (a dummy, `ok:false`); a connected-but-**failed** upload → `status:'error'` (previously swallowed into a fake `done`). Only a real post → `done`. - **Render honesty:** a stub render → `ContentAsset.status:'error'`, `downloadable:false`, and `RenderJob.status: 'error'` — it no longer masquerades as a `ready`, `downloadable` video. - **claude-CLI honesty:** `available()` now actually resolves the binary — `existsSync` for a path, a real `--version` probe (PATH-resolved, cached) for a bare name — so a not-installed CLI reports unavailable. - **A real proof:** `tests/live/renderLive.live.mts` (opt-in) generates real fal images + runs the real ffmpeg-in-Docker render and asserts a non-`stub://`, on-disk, non-triv

chunks.title: 0145-conversational-intake-copilot
chunks.text: ADR 0145: 0145-conversational-intake-copilot. The honest audit (`memory/workspaces-honest-gap-audit`) found the biggest gap to "just chat + approve → it happens": the Workspace-AI could only PROPOSE 3 board ops (bulk-move / assign / add-comment) — it could not CREATE anything, and content was a wall of manual generate-buttons with no conversational entry. There was no "make me X" front door. IDEA_TO_OUTCOME_PROGRAM Fase L2 (O-A/O-B) closes this, first, because it unblocks the whole "idea → outcome" feel for both the dev and content sides. Decision: - **O-B — the Assistant can now propose CREATE ops.** `ChatProposal.op` gains `create-ticket` and `create-content`. On accept they route to the EXISTING verbs — `create-ticket → workspaces/quickAdd`, `create-content → workspaces/contentControl` (`content-from-brief`). NO new verbs, NO new writers: the AI still only proposes; the user accepts; the Conductor writes (B-23 single-writer + the frozen structured-channel surface both intact). - **O-A — the IntakeCopilot: multi-step PLANS.** A big idea ("build a todo app with login") decomposes into an ordered `ChatPlan` of steps (each a `ChatProposal`), rendered as ONE approvable card; approving dispatches every step in order through the same single-step dispatch path. This is the distinct value over O-B's single op. - **Validation stays a hard guard.** `validateChatAction` / `validatePlan` (exported, unit-tested) drop any step that doesn't independently validate; a plan needs ≥2 survivin

chunks.title: 0146-video-scene-model
chunks.text: ADR 0146: 0146-video-scene-model. The audit found "video" was a still-image slideshow — no real multi-clip video, no timeline. IDEA_TO_OUTCOME Fase V builds real video; V1 is the data foundation the render (V2), long-video decompose (V3), range-refine (V4) and the timeline editor (V5) all sit on. The existing `Beat` model is a slideshow still bound to a script; it can't represent an ordered set of real clips with trims + transitions. Decision: - **New `VideoScene` model** (per content piece): `order`, `videoAssetId?` (a real clip) / `imageAssetId?` (a still/ken-burns fallback), `startTrimMs` / `endTrimMs`, `durationMs`, `transitionIn` (cut|fade|xfade), `prompt` (for V3/V4 regen) and `parentId` (I2-lineage — a refined version of a prior scene). - **`videoAssetId` / `imageAssetId` are plain `String?`, not `@db.ObjectId`.** A user-editable timeline must never hard-fail a whole save because one ref isn't a valid ObjectId; asset refs are soft. `parentId` stays `@db.ObjectId` (internal lineage, always a real scene id). - **One write op, `content-save-scenes`** (a `[control-API]` op via the contentControl route, RBAC `work-tickets`): the timeline editor sends the full ordered list; the Conductor UPSERTS by id (existing scenes keep their id + lineage, new ones are created, dropped ones removed) and re-sequences `order`. One op covers reorder/trim/transition/delete/add — matching how an editor saves. - **Surfaced in the read snapshot** (`ContentPieceSummary.scenes`) for the editor + t

chunks.title: 0147-multi-clip-video-render
chunks.text: ADR 0147: 0147-multi-clip-video-render. The audit's headline finding: "video" was a still-image slideshow (`buildFfmpegPlan` — one image per beat) and the only real video-gen clip was never used in the render. V1 added the `VideoScene` timeline model; V2 makes the render actually STITCH real clips, so a piece can become a real multi-scene video (the marquee of the "idea → outcome" work). Decision: - **`buildVideoStitchPlan(scenes, audioFile, outName, format)`** — a pure, exported ffmpeg-filter_complex plan that stitches real scenes: each scene is normalized to one uniform stream (a clip is `trim`med to its in/out-point; a still is `-loop`ed + time-bounded, then everything is scaled/fps/format-matched). Joining is a single exact `concat` when every transition is a hard cut, or an `xfade` chain when any scene crossfades in (offsets = the running composited length minus the transition, so fades overlap correctly).
