Optional audio is the last input, mapped + `-shortest`. - **`renderScenes(...)`** — the real-video render entry (mirrors `renderTimeline`): localizes each scene's clip/still + the voice, builds the stitch plan, runs the SAME injectable ffmpeg-in-Docker runner, typed degrade on failure. - **`assembly.ts` prefers scenes.** When the piece has a `VideoScene` timeline it renders THAT (real stitch); otherwise it falls back to the beat slideshow. The render metadata (`totalMs`, `sceneCount`) reflects whichever path ran.

chunks.title: 0148-long-video-decomposition
chunks.text: ADR 0148: 0148-long-video-decomposition. The user's flagship ask: "make a 60s video about X" should split into several shorter scenes that FLOW into each other, then stitch. V1 gave the scene model, V2 the stitch. V3 is the step that turns a piece's storyboard (script beats) into a generated, continuity-linked set of scenes. Decision: - **`buildContinuityPrompts(beats)`** (pure, tested): one prompt per beat, where every scene after the first is told to "continue seamlessly from the previous scene: <prev visual>", so consecutive clips are visually coherent. The first scene has no continuity hint; a beat with no `visualPrompt` falls back to its text. - **`decomposeIntoScenes(...)`** generates a clip per beat via the shared queue-aware media lifecycle (`runQueuedMediaAsset`, feature `video-gen` — a stub clip without a key), and creates a `VideoScene` linking it. Scenes after the first crossfade in (`transitionIn: 'xfade'`) so they flow together. Budget-guarded (partial on cap) and re-decomposing REPLACES the scene list. - **`content-decompose-video`** control-op (contentControl route, RBAC work-tickets): finds the piece's latest script and decomposes it; an optional `sceneDurationMs` sets the per-scene length.

chunks.title: 0149-range-refine
chunks.text: ADR 0149: 0149-range-refine. The user's editing vision: "select seconds 13–18 and say refine the transition / voice-over" — iterate a long video without redoing the whole thing. V1–V3 built the scene timeline, stitch, and decomposition; V4 is the targeted edit. Decision: - **`scenesInRange(scenes, startMs, endMs)`** (pure, tested): maps the ordered scenes onto a cumulative timeline and returns those whose interval overlaps the selected range (half-open `[start,end)`), each with its computed `startMs`/`endMs`. - **`refineSceneRange(...)`** regenerates every covered scene as a NEW version: a fresh `video-gen` clip with the instruction folded into the scene's prompt (`<prompt>. Refinement: <instruction>`), a new `VideoScene` with `parentId` = the old scene (I2 lineage) keeping the same order/duration/transition, then the old scene is removed — so the timeline keeps its shape and the edit is traceable. - **`content-refine-range`** control-op (contentControl route, RBAC work-tickets): `{ startMs, endMs, instruction }`; a range that hits no scene is a no-op.

chunks.title: 0150-youtube-byte-upload
chunks.text: ADR 0150: 0150-youtube-byte-upload. The audit's sharpest finding: a real YouTube publish never worked, even WITH OAuth keys. `realUploadTransport` did only the resumable INIT (a POST that returns the session URI in its `Location` header + an empty body), then read a video `id` from that empty body — always empty → null → the honesty-fixed publish (ADR 0144) recorded it as an `error`/stub. The actual video bytes were never sent. IDEA_TO_OUTCOME D1 closes that gap so a user with a real Google OAuth app can actually post a video. Decision: - **All three legs of the resumable upload.** `youtubeResumableUpload`: (1) POST the metadata (the existing `buildUploadRequest` init, which carries `X-Upload-Content-Type` so YouTube returns a session URI) and read the `Location` header; (2) read the video bytes; (3) PUT the bytes to the session URI and read the video `id` from the response. Any leg failing → null → the publish is an honest error (never a fake success). - **`buildResumablePut(sessionUri, accessToken)`** — a pure, exported builder for leg 3 (the transport attaches the byte body), unit-tested alongside the init builder. - **`readAssetBytes(assetUrl)`** — reads a local `/media/<file>` from the media store or fetches an http(s) URL; a `stub://`/unknown url yields null (not uploadable). So a real rendered mp4 in the media store uploads directly, without needing a public URL. - **TikTok stays a single init** (PULL_FROM_URL); its status-polling + confirmed url is D2.

chunks.title: 0151-tiktok-status-polling
chunks.text: ADR 0151: 0151-tiktok-status-polling. The audit found the TikTok publish fabricated a url: it did the `PULL_FROM_URL` init, got a `publish_id`, and returned `tiktok.com/@me/video/<publish_id>` with NO confirmation — but a `publish_id` is a job id, not a post id, and TikTok publishes asynchronously (the post only exists once the status endpoint reports complete). Decision: - **Poll the status endpoint until confirmed.** `tiktokUpload`: init → `publish_id` → poll `/post/publish/status/fetch/` (bounded, `TIKTOK_POLL_ATTEMPTS`) until `PUBLISH_COMPLETE`, then build the url from the CONFIRMED public post id. `FAILED` or not-confirmed-within-the-window → null (an honest error, per ADR 0144) — never a fabricated url. - **Pure builders/parser:** `buildTiktokStatusRequest(publishId, accessToken)` and `parseTiktokStatus(json)` (status enum + the public post id), unit-tested. The `sleep` between polls is injected so the live poll waits without affecting tests (which inject the whole transport).

chunks.title: 0152-content-pipeline-orchestration
chunks.text: ADR 0152: 0152-content-pipeline-orchestration. Even after V1–V4 (real video) the content side was still "a wall of manual generate buttons" — the user had to fire script, then voice, then images/decompose, then assemble, one at a time. The "idea → outcome" promise needs a single run that turns a brief into a complete piece. O-A lets the Assistant CREATE a content piece; O-C makes it actually PRODUCE the video. Decision: - **`runContentPipeline(...)`** chains the existing step functions — `generateScript` → `generateVoiceover` → (`decomposeIntoScenes` for `mode:'video'` | `generateBeatImages` for `mode:'slideshow'`) → `assembleContent` — into one run. It reuses an existing script rather than regenerating (idempotent-ish), threads the real `scriptId`, and returns which steps ran + whether any output stubbed. NO new generation logic — it composes the reviewed step functions. - **`content-run-pipeline`** control-op (contentControl route, RBAC work-tickets): `{ contentProjectId, mode? }`; `video` is the default (the marquee stitched-scene path). - The run itself is the user's consent (B-23); per-step autonomy-gating (pause for approval between stages, reusing the autonomy dial) is a logged follow-up.

chunks.title: 0153-video-timeline-editor
chunks.text: ADR 0153: 0153-video-timeline-editor. V1–V4 built the whole backend of an editable multi-scene video (scene model, stitch render, decomposition, range-refine) but the only way to drive it was raw control-ops. V5 is the editor a user actually operates; V6 (split/delete/transition) folds into it because those are just edits to the scene list the editor saves. Decision: - **`VideoTimelineEditor`** (modal from the content piece page): renders the piece's `VideoScene`s as proportional blocks and drives the existing ops — edit a scene's **duration (trim)** + **transition** (Dropdown), **split** (halve a scene → a new second half), **delete**, **reorder** (left/right) → all saved as the full ordered list via `content-save-scenes` (upsert by id, so ids/lineage survive). A **range selector** (start/end seconds + instruction) fires `content-refine-range`; a **"Generate scenes"** button fires `content-decompose-video`. Every write goes through `runContentOp` → the Conductor (B-23). - **`runContentOp` payload widened to `Record<string, unknown>`** so the editor can pass the scene array + numeric start/end (not just strings); the route validates each op's real shape server-side. - **Reorder/split/trim are buttons + inputs, not raw drag.** They are reliable, keyboard-accessible, and produce exactly the same scene-list save; drag is a logged follow-up (it needs live browser tuning).

chunks.title: 0154-auto-activation
chunks.text: ADR 0154: 0154-auto-activation. To start the AI on a new ticket the user had to create it (lands at `unrefined`, AI off) and then MANUALLY drag it into the first AI stage. IDEA_TO_OUTCOME O-D removes that step for the common "I want the AI on this now" case. Decision: - **`quick-add` gains an optional `startWithAi` flag.** The ticket still ENTERS at `unrefined` (the invariant "a user-created ticket always enters at unrefined; no client can place it mid-pipeline" is preserved — the Conductor is the writer). Then, when `startWithAi` is set, the Conductor advances it to the FIRST `aiEnabled` stage, records a `status-change` event ("auto-started AI at <stage>"), and runs `activateWorktreesForStage` (a no-op without a linked repo/Docker, as usual). It returns the ADVANCED row so the realtime delta shows the new stage. - **Wired end to end:** the `workspaces/quickAdd` route threads `startWithAi`; the client `quickAdd` helper + the New-ticket form expose a checkbox ("Start with AI right away", i18n ×4).

chunks.title: 0155-image-crop-resize
chunks.text: ADR 0155: 0155-image-crop-resize. The image editor already did adjustments (B/C/S), one-tap looks (B3), and a text overlay (B2), all as non-destructive Fabric-canvas edits exported to a NEW asset via the tested `content-import-asset` flow. B1 adds the two remaining "essentials" the program calls for — crop and resize-to-preset — without leaving that client-side, no-provider model. Decision: - **Crop is a draggable/resizable Fabric `Rect`** toggled on: its `getBoundingRect()` (clamped to the canvas by the pure `clampCropRegion`) becomes the exported sub-region via Fabric's `toDataURL({left,top,width,height})`. The rect is removed before export so it isn't baked into the output. - **Resize is a preset dropdown** (`Original / 1080 / 720 / 512` px width) applied after crop through an offscreen 2D-canvas draw sized by the pure `resizeDimensions` (shrink-only, aspect-preserving). - **The geometry lives in a Fabric-free helper** (`_functions/imageCrop.ts`) so `clampCropRegion` (clamp, invert-normalise, degenerate→null) and `resizeDimensions` are unit-tested without a canvas (11/11). - **No new op, no provider, no spend.** Export still goes through the existing upload + `content-import-asset` path (B-23: the Conductor writes the asset), identical to B2/B3.

chunks.title: 0156-structured-approvals
chunks.text: ADR 0156: 0156-structured-approvals. When an in-container agent blocked on a question it emitted a `ws-needs-input` block. Two problems: (1) the parsed questions were **dropped** — `stageRunner` parked the session busy but never wrote the question onto the ticket, so the human saw nothing; (2) even the defer-message banner was a single free-text input, so a yes/no or pick-one decision meant typing prose on a phone. P-B makes the agent's question actually surface, and as a structured, tap-to-answer card. Decision: - **Encode structure inside the existing `needsInput` string — no schema change, no new verb.** A FREE question stays its plain prompt (every existing reader — banner, answer-queue, `isRealNeedsInput` — is unaffected); an APPROVE or CHOICE question is stored as a compact `@@wsq:` JSON envelope. The pure, isomorphic `structuredQuestion.ts` (`encodeQuestion` / `parseStructuredQuestion` / `questionPrompt`) is the single wire-shape source shared by server and client. - **Close the surfacing gap in `stageRunner`.** On a needs-input turn, persist the first question (already needsInput-encoded by `parseTurnResult`) onto the ticket + flip it to `needs-input` + broadcast, so the board/phone renders the card. `parseTurnResult` now accepts structured entries (`{prompt,kind,options}`) alongside bare strings. - **The card (`NeedsInputBanner`) renders by kind:** approve → Approve/Reject (+ optional note); choice → one tap-target per option; free → the text input. Every path routes

chunks.title: 0157-prod-build-export-deploy-hook
chunks.text: ADR 0157: 0157-prod-build-export-deploy-hook. `build-export` produced only a `docker save` image tarball; the `bundle` kind (a real production build, `npm run build` → dist/) returned `export.bundleNotImplemented`. And there was no way to hand a built artifact to an external server — the "prod = CI/CD to another host" half of the idea→outcome vision. D4 implements both, on the existing Docker + BuildArtifact + signed-download plumbing (no new op — `build-export` already exists and is RBAC-gated). Decision: - **Bundle export runs the REAL build inside a throwaway container from the project image**: `docker run` `<buildCmd> && tar -czf /tmp/bundle.tgz -C <outputDir> .`, then `docker cp` the single tarball out, then `docker rm -f`. Build + tar happen IN the container (the app image has node + tar/gzip), so nothing is assumed about the host — it works cross-platform (the host never tars). `buildCmd`/`outputDir` are read from env at CALL time (`WS_BUILD_EXPORT_CMD` default `cd /app && npm run build`, `WS_BUILD_EXPORT_DIR` default `/app/dist`) so a non-standard project pins its own build without a code change or restart. - **The deploy-hook is a webhook POST** of a self-describing descriptor (`event, workspaceId, projectId, kind, artifactId, imageRef, downloadToken`) to `WS_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL` (+ optional bearer), fired automatically after a ready artifact. The fetch is injectable (`DeployFetch`) so it is E2E-tested against a real local HTTP receiver. Unconfigured → `fired:false` n

chunks.title: 0158-demo-host-auto-redeploy
chunks.text: ADR 0158: 0158-demo-host-auto-redeploy. The deploy engine already runs a project's target branch (main) at a stable route (`<kind>-<slug>.<domain>`) via Caddy + Docker. What was missing for "main draait op DNS X" as a demo surface: a dedicated demo kind and the thing that makes a demo useful — it stays current as main advances, or is deliberately frozen at a commit for a stable link. Decision: - **A `demo` env kind** (added to `ENV_KINDS`) that reuses the whole existing deploy path (clone target branch → serve → readiness → flip the stable route). No parallel deploy engine. - **Three fields on `Environment`** (MongoDB — no migration): `deployedCommit` (what the current deploy runs), `autoRedeploy` (follow main), `pinnedCommit` (freeze at a fixed commit; disables auto-redeploy and is `git checkout`'d in the container so the demo serves that exact commit). - **A leader-gated `demoWatch` sweep** (`startDemoWatcher`, same shape as the cron/publish schedulers): every tick it resolves each demo env's target-branch head (`branchHead`) and redeploys when it moved. The decision is the pure `shouldRedeployDemo` (auto on + not pinned + known head + head ≠ deployed); head-resolution and deploy are injectable so the sweep is tested with injected git-state, no git/container needed. - **`ensureEnvironment` defaults a demo to autoRedeploy=true** unless a `pinnedCommit` is given (a pin always wins); `env-deploy` passes `pinnedCommit`/`autoRedeploy` through. No new op.

chunks.title: 0159-greenfield-repo-gen
chunks.text: ADR 0159: 0159-greenfield-repo-gen. `project-from-template` created a Project row + seeded convention docs + a default pipeline, but never made a REPO — `gitlabPath:''`, no `gitUrl`, no bare clone. So `isLinked` stayed false, the runtime couldn't cut a worktree, and no container/code followed. A "greenfield" project was a shell with nothing to edit. G1 makes it a real, runnable starting point with no external forge. Decision: - **Templates carry a seed `files` tree** (`StarterFile[]`) — a minimal but runnable skeleton per stack (package.json + entry + config + README + .gitignore for node-api / react-vite; requirements.txt + app/main .py for fastapi). Not a full app: the starting point the impl-stage agent fleshes out. - **`initGreenfieldRepo(workspaceId, files)` in repoStore** writes the tree into a temp checkout, `git init -b main` + a self-contained identity + commit, then `git clone --bare` into the durable per-workspace `repo.git`. `isLinked` flips true → the existing worktree/container path just works (container → code). It is a **no-op when a repo already exists** (never clobber a linked repo), and self-contained (no external forge, no network). - **`project-from-template` calls it best-effort** and stamps the project `gitUrl: greenfield://<workspaceId>` when it linked, so the UI/status treats it as a linked project. A git failure logs + leaves the project unlinked (the row + pipeline still exist).

chunks.title: 0160-greenfield-wizard-ui
chunks.text: ADR 0160: 0160-greenfield-wizard-ui. G1 made `project-from-template` produce a real repo, and both `createFromTemplate` (provider) and the `templates` catalog (snapshot) were already exposed — but nothing in the UI rendered them, so a user could never pick a stack template. G2 is the front door onto the greenfield op. Decision: - **Extend the existing `CreateProjectForm`** (the "New project" menu off the project switcher) with a two-mode toggle: **From a template** (greenfield — a stack-template picker → `createFromTemplate`, which runs G1's real-repo init) and **Link a repo** (the pre-existing name + git-URL → `createProject`). Template mode is the default (greenfield-first). - **The picker is driven by the snapshot `templates`** (label + description cards, single-select). Submit branches on mode; the create button disables until a name (and, in template mode, a template) is chosen. - **No new op, no new screen file.** The wizard is the create-project menu the switcher already opens, so it works for the first project and every later one.

chunks.title: 0161-timeline-audio-track
chunks.text: ADR 0161: 0161-timeline-audio-track. V5's timeline editor shipped scenes + trim + transitions + range-refine, but the spec's last piece — "een audio-spoor met de E4-waveform + volume/duck-sliders" — was missing, and the render only ever mixed the voiceover (music + per-track gains were unreachable). This closes that gap so a user can see and balance the audio and have it actually affect the rendered video. Decision: - **Per-piece mix on `ContentProject`** (MongoDB, no migration): `voiceVolume` (default 1) + `musicVolume` (default 0.25, ducked). Persisted by a new **`content-save-audio-mix`** control-op (content-* write family; no new frozen verb) — RBAC `workTickets`, clamped (voice ≤ 2, music ≤ 1) by the Conductor (B-23). - **The render honours the gains.** `buildVideoStitchPlan` gained an optional `mix` ({musicFile, voiceVolume, musicVolume}); when there's music OR a non-default voice gain it routes voice (+ ducked music) through the existing `buildAudioMixPlan` (E4) → `[aout]`. **Guarded** so the plain single-voice path is byte-identical — the live render test is unchanged (re-run 7/7). `renderScenes` + `assembly` thread the piece's music asset + gains in. - **The snapshot surfaces** `voiceVolume`/`musicVolume` + the newest voice/music asset urls on `ContentPieceSummary`, so the editor can draw the track without another fetch. - **A real waveform** in `VideoTimelineEditor`: `decodePeaks` fetches + `decodeAudioData` → per-block peak bars on a canvas, theme-driven (fillStyle

chunks.title: Q1 — product self-knowledge corpus (generator)
chunks.text: ADR 0250: Q1 — product self-knowledge corpus (generator). The in-app Workspace-AI grounds only on the workspace snapshot + the user's linked code (RAG). It has ZERO knowledge of what the PRODUCT itself can do, so it cannot answer "can we edit videos?" ("yes — via the media module, first generate/upload a video then use the timeline editor"). The rich self-knowledge (161 ADRs + the capability inventory) exists as committed docs but is only reachable by the dev-time `@luckystack/mcp` server, never at runtime. Q1 compiles that knowledge into a retrievable corpus. > **ADR numbering:** this program (`AI_LIBRARIES_ACCOUNTS_PROGRAM.md`) runs on the `feat/ai-libraries-accounts` > branch in parallel with the ADOPTION run, which consumes 0162+. To avoid merge-time number collisions, this > program's ADRs start at **0250**. Decision: - **A hand-curated capability Q&A** (`docs/product-knowledge/capabilities.md`) is the primary source: plain- language "can I do X? → yes, via module Y, steps ..." blocks, one `### Q:` per capability. This is what makes the AI genuinely helpful ("how do I ...") rather than just factual. - **A deterministic generator** (`scripts/generateProductKnowledge.mjs`, `npm run ai:product-knowledge`, wired into the pre-commit hook) compiles the Q&A + every ADR (title + Context/Decision summary) into two artifacts: `docs/AI_PRODUCT_KNOWLEDGE.md` (human digest) + `docs/AI_PRODUCT_KNOWLEDGE.json` (`{hash, chunks:[{id,kind,title,text}]}` — the embedding input). Pure-Node,

chunks.title: Q2 — product-knowledge RAG corpus (global, behind the existing retrieve)
chunks.text: ADR 0251: Q2 — product-knowledge RAG corpus (global, behind the existing retrieve). Q1 compiled the product's self-knowledge into `docs/AI_PRODUCT_KNOWLEDGE.json` (capability Q&A + ADR summaries). Q2 makes it retrievable at chat-time so the Workspace-AI can answer capability questions. The RAG store (`RagEntry` + `retrieve()`) already exists and is reused twice for non-code corpora (institutional memory, per-channel brand) via a sentinel "commit" — this is the third instance. Decision: - **`server/rag/productKnowledge.ts`** indexes the compiled corpus into `RagEntry` under a GLOBAL scope: a reserved sentinel `workspaceId` = the zero ObjectId `000000000000000000000000` (no real workspace) + a sentinel `commitHash` = `product-knowledge`. `retrieveProductKnowledge(prisma, query, k)` = `retrieve(..., PRODUCT_WS, ..., PRODUCT_COMMIT)`, excluding a meta/marker row. Reuses the one embedder + the one cosine scan — no parallel retrieval path. - **Idempotent on the corpus hash.** A marker row (`__product_meta__`) records the indexed hash; the boot `ensureProductKnowledge` re-embeds only when the corpus changed. Indexed once at boot, leader-gated + delayed so leadership has settled; best-effort (never blocks/breaks boot). - **Deterministic + offline-testable.** In the default test world the LOCAL embedder (no GEMINI key) is used, so the E2E is deterministic and free: "can I edit videos?" retrieves the media/timeline-editor chunk.

chunks.title: Q3 — wire product self-knowledge into the Workspace-AI + every feature
chunks.text: ADR 0252: Q3 — wire product self-knowledge into the Workspace-AI + every feature. Q1 compiled the product's self-knowledge and Q2 made it retrievable, but nothing consumed it yet. Q3 wires it into the in-app AI so it actually answers "can we edit videos?" from the corpus. Decision: - **`workspaceChat.interpretChat` retrieves the product corpus** (`retrieveProductKnowledge(message, 4)`) alongside the existing code-RAG, and injects it into the system prompt as a SEPARATE "What THIS product can do" section — deliberately distinct from the user-code section so the model never confuses product capabilities with the user's repository. A new instruction tells it to answer whether/how questions from that section (name the module + steps) and, when a first step maps to an op, propose it. - **A compact global capability index in `registry.workspaceAiPrefix`/`runAiCompletion`** — the capability TITLES (not the full corpus), read once from the compiled shard + cached, prepended to EVERY feature's system prompt at the single choke-point. So the whole AI surface is product-aware, cheaply (~15 lines), with the detail retrieved on demand in chat. - **B-23 unchanged.** The assistant still only proposes; the Conductor is the single writer.

chunks.title: L1 — premade UI-look gallery (curated combos over the existing seeds)
chunks.text: ADR 0253: L1 — premade UI-look gallery (curated combos over the existing seeds). The Designer module already had the building blocks — palettes (DesignTheme), component styles (DesignStyle, incl. Apple/Material/Glass/Brutalist), animations, fonts — with live-preview via `themeVars`/`styleVars`. But there was no curated CATALOG of ready-made looks to browse + apply, and no rich preview surfaces (a real landing/menu/animation/font showcase). L1 adds that reference gallery. Decision: - **A premade-look catalog as curated COMBINATIONS of the existing seeds** (`premades.ts`): a "look" pairs a seed palette + a seed style + an animation + heading/body fonts. Eight starter looks (Apple, Material, Glass, Brutalist, Minimal, Editorial, Playful, Neumorphic) — a strong STARTER that upload/copy/customize (L3) extends. Pure data + a `resolveLook` resolver; no new palette authoring. - **A `Gallery` section** (now the Designer's default tab) renders the catalog as thumbnails and, for the selected look, live preview SURFACES under the look's vars: a nav menu, a landing hero, a card row, a replayable entrance animation (motion/react + the seed AnimSpec), and a font showcase. Tailwind colour classes inside the preview read the OVERRIDDEN `--color-*` vars, so the subtree re-themes; `--ds-*` drives the shapes. "Use this look" applies its theme + style via the existing persist path.

chunks.title: L2 — designer persistence round-trip (consume the snapshot's designArtifacts)
chunks.text: ADR 0254: L2 — designer persistence round-trip (consume the snapshot's designArtifacts). The Designer's libraries (themes/styles/anims) were client-held `useState` seeded from `SEED_*`. Saving a look wrote a `DesignArtifact` (save + setActive), but nothing loaded them BACK — persistence was one-directional, so a saved theme vanished on reload and never appeared in the gallery/rails. The snapshot already exposes the full `designArtifacts` rows (content included); they were consumed only for the active name. Decision: - **Consume the existing snapshot `designArtifacts` — no new `list`/`load` op.** The snapshot IS the list. `persisted.ts` parses each row back into the typed shape (`artifactToTheme`/`Style`/`Anim` + a `parsePersistedLibraries` splitter), defensively: a malformed/half-set row coerces to null (never crashes the designer). The content shapes match what `useInProject` writes (`{light,dark}` for a theme, the full spec for a style/anim). - **`state.tsx` merges the persisted artifacts into the libraries** via a `useEffect` on `designArtifacts`, appending by id (idempotent), never clobbering unsaved local edits. So a saved look reappears on reload AND live right after saving (refetch → the effect re-runs).

chunks.title: L3 — designer import / copy / customize / delete
chunks.text: ADR 0255: L3 — designer import / copy / customize / delete. L1 gave a premade-look gallery and L2 the persistence round-trip. L3 lets a user make the library their own: copy a premade into their workspace, import a theme/style JSON, customize it, and delete their own. Decision: - **Copy a premade → workspace artifacts.** `lookToArtifacts(resolved)` produces a theme artifact (its palette) + a style artifact (its component spec with the look's fonts baked in), saved via the existing `designerLibrary` `save` op. They round-trip (L2) into the editable rails, so "copy" = "make it mine". - **Import a theme/style/anim JSON.** A file picker in the gallery reads the JSON, and **`validArtifactContent` (pure, reuses the L2 coercion) refuses anything that isn't a real theme/style/anim** before saving — a garbage upload can't poison the library. Reuses `save`; no new op. - **Customize + delete reuse existing surfaces.** Rail edits (rename/duplicate/token-edit) now persist through L2; delete is the existing per-workspace `deleteDesignArtifact` (premades/seeds stay read-only).

chunks.title: M2 — thread the style through the video path (decompose)
chunks.text: ADR 0256: M2 — thread the style through the video path (decompose). Picking a style ("stick-man figures") only affected the SLIDESHOW path (per-beat images all styled). The real-video path was ungenerated-style: `runContentPipeline` did not pass its `opts` to `decomposeIntoScenes`, and `decomposeIntoScenes` had no `styleKey` param — it sent each scene's beat prompt with NO `style`. So a styled video request produced unstyled clips. This is the single highest-value content fix in the program. Decision: - **`decomposeIntoScenes` resolves the piece's `video-gen` style and rides it on every scene request.** It gained `styleKey`/`extraInstructions` params, calls `resolveStyle(ws, 'video-gen', styleKey)`, and passes `request.style` + `styleId` — the exact pattern `images.ts` already uses for the slideshow path. - **`buildSceneRequest` is extracted (pure + exported)** so a unit test asserts the style rides every scene- gen request, deterministically. - **The wiring is completed end-to-end:** `runContentPipeline` now forwards `...opts` to `decomposeIntoScenes`, and the two conductor ops (`content-run-pipeline`, `content-decompose-video`) forward `styleKey` + `extraInstructions` from the payload.

chunks.title: M1 — style preview asset + thumbnail affordance
chunks.text: ADR 0257: M1 — style preview asset + thumbnail affordance. Media styles were a text-only list (label + systemPrompt) picked from a name dropdown — nothing showed a sample of the LOOK, so a user couldn't say "I like THIS look". `StylePreset.params` already existed; only a preview reference was missing. Decision: - **Two nullable columns on `StylePreset`**: `previewAssetUrl` (a sample image/video of the style) + `previewKind` ('image'|'video') — MongoDB, no migration. Threaded through `listStyles` (ResolvedStyle), the `save-style` op, and the snapshot's `content.styles`, so a style carries its preview end to end. - **The picker shows the chosen style's preview** (a looping muted `

chunks.title: M3 — pick-a-look + long-form video duration planner
chunks.text: ADR 0258: M3 — pick-a-look + long-form video duration planner. The pipeline emitted a fixed 4–8 beats → ~20–40s videos; there was no way to ask for a longer video, and "pick a look + topic → make a video" needed the style to reach the video path (M2, done). M3 adds the duration planner so "a 10-minute video about the moon landing in stick-man figures" is expressible. Decision: - **A pure `planBeatCount(targetDurationMs, sceneDurationMs)`** maps a target duration to ~N beats/scenes (each ≈ sceneDuration), bounded to [2, `MAX_BEATS` = 40]. The media budget stays the true hard cap; 40 is the planner ceiling so a runaway target can't fan out to hundreds of paid clips. - **`generateScript` gained `targetBeats`** → `scriptFormat(targetBeats)` asks the model for ~N beats, and the stub script yields exactly N (deterministic in the stub world). `runContentPipeline` gained `durationMs` + `sceneDurationMs`, plans the beat count, threads it to the script + the per-scene length to decompose. The `content-run-pipeline` op forwards both. - **A Length picker** (Auto / Short / Normal / Long) on the piece page sets `durationMs`; combined with the M1 style picker, that IS "pick a look + a length → make a video". 0 = auto (the default arc).

chunks.title: M4 — media-style upload / copy / customize / delete (preview-aware)
chunks.text: ADR 0259: M4 — media-style upload / copy / customize / delete (preview-aware). M1 gave styles a preview asset + params. The style CRUD (save-style/delete-style) and the portable style-set export/import already existed, but were TEXT-ONLY — a copied/shared style lost its preview. M4 makes the whole CRUD + portability preview-aware. Decision: - **`save-style` + `delete-style` already do create/customize/delete** per-workspace (builtins stay read-only); M1 made `save-style` accept `previewAssetUrl`/`previewKind`. - **The portable style-set carries the preview.** `StyleSetEntry` + `parseStyleSet` + `exportStyleSet` + `importStyleSet` gained `previewAssetUrl`/`previewKind`, so export → parse → import preserves the look. This is the "copy/share a style and keep its look" path. - **Copy a builtin into the workspace = a `save-style` pre-filled** from the gallery/builtin entry (a new key, editable) — reusing the existing op, no new surface.

chunks.title: A1+A2 — multi-account connections + channel management
chunks.text: ADR 0260: A1+A2 — multi-account connections + channel management. Publishing stored ONE token per platform (`__publish_<platform>`), so connecting a second YouTube account overwrote the first; and channels (a platform + brand identity) could only be created in tests — no create/edit/delete op or UI. A1+A2 make "manage all your social accounts + channels via the workspace" real. Decision: - **A1 — re-key the connection store** so `tokenKey(platform, accountId?)` = `__publish_<platform>` (default, back-compat) or `__publish_<platform>_<accountId>` for N accounts per platform. `saveConnection`/ `getConnection` gained an optional `accountId`. The token-refresh logic (ADOPTION F1) stays orthogonal — this only changes the KEY, not the read/refresh. - **A2 — channel + account management ops** (content-* write family, RBAC): `channel-create`/`channel-edit`/ `channel-delete` (a channel = projectId + name + platform + handle + brandVoice + defaultStyleId) and `account-disconnect` (remove a connected account's token by platform + optional accountId). Channels are already on the snapshot; the CRUD makes them user-managed.

chunks.title: A3+A4 — publish routing by account + content bound to a channel
chunks.text: ADR 0261: A3+A4 — publish routing by account + content bound to a channel. A1+A2 gave N accounts per platform + channel management. A3 makes a publish target a CHOSEN account (not just "the platform"), and A4 lets a content piece be created bound to a channel ("make a video for channel Z") so generation grounds on that channel's brand. Decision: - **A3 — thread `accountId` through the publish path.** `performUpload` + `publishAsset` gained an optional `accountId` → `getConnection(platform, accountId)`, so the upload uses the chosen account's token (default account when omitted). `content-request-publish` carries `accountId` in the suggestion patch; the accept passes it to `publishAsset`. - **A4 — `content-from-brief` accepts `channelId`.** The created `ContentProject` is bound to the channel (content-create already did), so `brandContext` + brand-RAG ground every generation on that channel's voice. The Workspace-AI can propose "make a video for channel Z" by re-expressing it as a content-create/ content-from-brief with the channelId (no new verb).

chunks.title: Best-practices playbook — domain-expertise RAG grounding content generation
chunks.text: ADR 0262: Best-practices playbook — domain-expertise RAG grounding content generation. The content AI knew what the PRODUCT can do (product-knowledge corpus) and HOW to render (styles), but not what makes content WORK — hooks, retention structure, thumbnail principles, ad structure, per-platform rules. So a generated script was on-brand but not necessarily good. Domain craft was missing. Decision: - **A curated `docs/content-playbook/playbook.md`** holds platform-agnostic craft knowledge, one retrievable chunk per `###` section (hooks, scripts/retention, thumbnails, per-platform, ads). - **A fourth global RAG corpus** (`server/rag/contentPlaybook.ts`) — same second-corpus pattern as product-knowledge/memory/brand: the ONE embedder + the ONE `retrieve()`, global zero-ObjectId sentinel workspace, distinct commit `content-playbook`, idempotent on a content hash, boot-ensured leader-gated. The markdown is chunked at RUNTIME (no compiled JSON / generator needed — it's small + hand-curated). - **`generateScript` grounds on it**: retrieves the top-3 best-practices relevant to the brief and injects them as a "Proven content best-practices (apply these)" section in the system prompt, alongside brand + knowledge.

chunks.title: Inspiration/reference library — collect examples the AI emulates
chunks.text: ADR 0263: Inspiration/reference library — collect examples the AI emulates. Styles say HOW output renders and the best-practices playbook says what works in GENERAL, but there was no way for a workspace to say "make it like THESE examples" — the great ads/thumbnails/intros they've collected. That concrete, per-workspace inspiration was missing. Decision: - **A `ReferenceExample` model** (kind, title, `description` = why it works, optional `assetUrl`, tags). The human-written `description` is the grounding signal: a text model can't see the asset, so the "why it works" IS the inspiration; the asset is the visual shown in the library. - **Per-workspace RAG under commit `reference`** (`server/content/referenceLibrary.ts`) — mirrors brandMemory: one embedder, one `retrieve()`, indexed INCREMENTALLY (add → embed one row keyed by the example id; delete → remove that row). No global corpus (inspiration is the workspace's own). - **`generateScript` grounds on it**: retrieves the top-2 examples relevant to the brief and injects them as "Reference examples … emulate the APPROACH/structure, do NOT copy verbatim", alongside best-practices + brand. - **Ops** `reference-add`/`reference-delete` (content-* family, RBAC); the asset uploads via the existing media upload route → `assetUrl`. The snapshot exposes `content.references` for the library UI.

chunks.title: Named design looks + references in the agent prompts
chunks.text: ADR 0264: Named design looks + references in the agent prompts. The `design-system` context-doc the coding agent reads carried ONLY the active theme + style, so a ticket "build the dropdown in the Apple style" couldn't ground on Apple unless Apple was the active system. And the content-script prompt's best-practices/reference injection was retrieval-tested but the INJECTION itself was never asserted (stub mode discards the prompt). The user wants named references always available in prompts. Decision: - **A named-looks catalog in the design-system doc.** `buildDesignSystemDoc` now appends a catalog of every named look — the built-in premades (apple/material/…) AND the workspace's saved themes/styles — with each look's distinguishing tokens (primary/bg/text colours, radius, fonts, motion). So the agent can build in ANY named look, not just the active one. - **Premades come from a compiled JSON.** `scripts/generateDesignPremades.mjs` reads the client premade definitions (they only import types, so a tsx script can load them) → `docs/AI_DESIGN_PREMADES.json`, which the server reads. No client→server duplication; regenerate with `npm run ai:design-premades`. - **The doc exists from day one.** `rebuildDesignSystemDoc` is seeded on workspace creation and refreshed on every save/delete/setActive (not only setActive), so the named looks are available even before the user opens the Designer, and saved looks join/leave the catalog immediately. - **`generateScript.complete` is injectabl
